### 32.33 The rail planes and the node bars were on phantom nets, 4 Sep 2026, 18:54 (found by a gateway session, read-only)

A gateway session compared the DRC reports of the 17:49 deliverables with their predecessors and asked why the In2 rail plane went from 0 isolated islands on B11 to 195 on B12 with the same layout, and why A19 carried 28 zones_intersect errors. The first question had a hard answer. In the board file a schematic local label lands as `/NAME` and a power symbol as `NAME`. On A17 and B11 the rail was the power symbol `+5V`, so the generators' pours found it. The respin renamed the rail to the local label `+5V_M1`, the pour helper asked the board for `+5V_M1`, found nothing, and created an empty net of that name rather than failing. The In2 rail plane on both boards therefore belonged to a net with no pads at all, which DRC reports only as isolated copper. The same helper built the CELL+ and CELL_N node bars, the fuse and pin taps and the CELL+ In2 pour on A19, and the DC_N, SHORE_12V, PV_P and TRK_OUT pours on E4: all dead copper. Every pad was still connected, because the router routes the planes' nets as ordinary nets, so DRC showed 0 unrouted and the contract check passed while the rail and the pack node ran on the router's tracks alone, 0.4 mm and 1.0 mm wide, against 3 A rails and a 10 A node. Not a cosmetic count.

**Fix, all in the generators.** The pour helper now resolves the plain name and the `/` form and refuses to pour on a net that is not in the netlist. The taps of the node bars sit at priority 3 above the bars at 2, which removes the 28 intersecting-zone errors (same-net zones on one layer must carry distinct priorities). A new gate, `tools/check_zone_nets.py`, runs in every chain before the route and blocks it if any zone's net has no pads or two same-net zones on a layer share a priority. A19, B12 and E4 were regenerated and rerouted on the corrected pours (results appended below). The gateway session also noticed that every deliverable's `README-fab.txt` was a copy of PCB-B's, wrong on size, layers and assembly side for five of six boards since A15; `export_jlc.sh` now writes it from the board file.

**Lesson for the record.** A zone that lands on the wrong net is invisible to every check that counts connections, because the router makes the connections without it. Isolated-copper counts are the only symptom, and the project had rightly learned to read them as cosmetic. The count itself is not the signal; a jump from 0 to 195 on one zone in one revision is, and so is a zone whose net has no pads, which is what the gate now asks directly.

**Results of the rerun (4 Sep, night, appended).** B12 finished clean on the real-net planes: 0 hard, 0 unrouted, 276 vias and no isolated copper (195 islands before). E4 clean, 142 vias. A19 came back from the router with two open I2C connections at the charger, and the reason was structural, not the router's mood: the BQ25792 (`U20`, QFN-29 at 0.4 mm pitch) had no pre-route escapes on any pin, because `escape.py` rejects an escape via that sits within 0.75 mm of another part's pad and the 1210 input capacitor C60 stands 1.7 mm past the south row's tips. The router then boxed pin 15 (SDA) in with the TS_CHG track and the GND fanout via, and no via site existed on any layer within reach of the pad (the In1 REGN run, the In2 BTST2 run and the 0.8 mm GND via close every candidate; a manual attempt was reverted after 3 shorting items). Four generator fixes, none on the board file: the fan escape retries with the lane rule at 0.35 mm, a 0.7 mm via row and shallower depths when a neighbour sits past the row, its knees nest 0.15 mm deeper per pin toward the row centre so the second pin's splay clears the first pin's turn (a 0.4 mm row's second pin sat 0.14 mm from it and was always rejected), every escape is locked so KiCad exports it as `(type fix)` and Freerouting keeps it (unlocked escapes were ripped up), and the dangling-via clean-up keeps a via that a same-net track passes over (it had removed the stub router's closing via on an In2 run, which reopened HEAT_FLT after the finish). The stub router also gained the joining via for an inner-layer source and for a path that changes layer half-way. A19 pass 5: four attempts all at 0 hard and 1 open, 491 vias with 558 locked escape items, the last net closed by the stub router; finished 0 hard, 0 unrouted, no isolated copper. E5 rebuilt from it. `tools/check_contracts.py`: ALL CONTRACTS PASS. Deliverables, order notes and review prints committed from the laptop (d7c3e64, 733a6a5).

### 32.34 The panel becomes the case's weather face: sealed construction C5, owner rulings 4 Sep 2026, about 19:40 (section written 22:18)

**Ruling.** The owner: "make the field-kit IP68 ... the top PCB and its components MUST survive rain and dust and for no reason water must slip into the case passing through the top PCB." Asked for the target the panel is designed and tested to, the owner chose the IP67-class construction: every penetration of the face sealed against rain, dust, hose-down and temporary immersion with the lid open, the closed case keeping Peli's own IP67 (the 1520 is IP67 by the lid gasket; no Peli document rates the frame or the panel). Second ruling, the display seal against the 2 Sep rule of 14.6 (glass at most 0.8 mm proud on 0.05 mm transfer tape, "anything thicker breaks the limit"): the lens is sealed on a continuous closed-cell foam tape frame on its printed border and ends about 1.1 to 1.2 mm proud; the rest of 14.6 stands (one board, no screws, the display held by its tape). The kit is not labelled IP68 because the case's own rating is IP67; the intent, no water through the top PCB, is met by construction and will be shown by the bench procedure below, not claimed.

**What C4 had.** 335 plated holes crossed the 2.0 mm panel: 226 vias (48 of them at 0.25 mm, under the 0.3 mm the line was ordered with), 32 LED legs, 27 switch flying-lead pads, the sounder's two legs and the e-paper header on the face, the ribbon header's 20 pins and the two XH leads' four pins. Nothing sealed the panel to the frame: Peli's gasket sits between frame and case rim, the panel clamps to the frame's 10.9 mm bearing ring from below and its edge stops 1.05 to 1.2 mm short of the skirt. The display sat on 0.05 mm transfer tape, which bonds and does not seal. The e-paper window's long edges were an open slot (the module overhangs them by 0.1 mm and only the two end lands are taped). The APEM K seal needs a keyed hole and the board had round ones. Found on the way: `J_PANEL` at (208, 75) rotated 90 ran its rows along X, its shroud reached X 225, four mm past the panel edge and into the frame skirt, and eight of its holes sat under the bearing ring; the three toggle holes stood at Y 39.5, -2.5 and -44.5 instead of 42, 0 and -42 because the placer centred the asymmetric footprint by its bounding box; the "guard closed = safe" legend outlived the guards of 32.10; the AT401A boot named for the LIGHT toggle is a 12 mm-bushing part and does not fit the 1/4-40 D3 bushing (the fitting boot is AT428H); and BUILD.md and ASSEMBLY.md pocketed a lid foam that the 3 Sep purchase does not include.

**Construction (C5), one board, every seal a named part.** (1) Display: die-cut frame of 3M VHB 5915 (0.4 mm closed-cell acrylic foam, "seal against water" on its sheet, `vendor/seals/`), 5.25 mm wide on the west band, up to 13 mm on the east, inner edge 0.5 mm outside the aperture and outer edge 0.3 mm inside the glass edge; the band on the panel carries no copper on either layer (25.4 kept, the pour now excluded too). Lens 1.1 mm proud. (2) E-paper: a 2.0 mm UV-grade uncoated polycarbonate lens 107.2 x 66.6 R3 over the window on a 6.0 mm wide frame of the same tape with 3M Primer 94 on the lens (3M's UL listing of 5915 is on primer-coated polycarbonate); the research found that every hard-coated sheet at 1.5 mm is coated on both faces and its maker states adhesives do not adhere, and one-side coated sheet starts at 3 mm, so the prototype takes the plain UV grade. A 1.0 mm plate spanning 54 mm deflects about 1.5 mm under a 10 N finger press and would touch the glass; 2.0 mm deflects 0.19 mm into the 1.4 mm gap. The lens ends 2.4 mm above the face, 7.2 mm under the frame top. **R1 is retired**: the sealed window makes the flush glass moot and the ring's 0.1 mm web could not be fabricated. (3) C&K ATP19 / ATP16: IP67 switches whose hardware is a nut and an internal O-ring only (their sheets), so each gets a die-cut 1.0 mm Silex GP60 silicone washer under the bezel (ID hole + 0.3, OD the bezel). (4) NKK M2044SD3A01: the D3 bushing is IP67 with O-rings inside and outside and ships with one nut and one O-ring (spare AT516); the hole becomes the maker's D cut-out (6.5 with the flat at 5.8, A58), flat toward +X because NKK's keyway lies on the throw axis (A72) and the D flat is 90 degrees from it; boot AT428H. (5) APEM 5636ADKB-2V: the K option's O-ring and U360 gasket seal on the face under the front nut; the hole gets the K cut-out, 6.50 with a 2.70 x 1.10 keyway notch (A40), toward the operator, because APEM's bushing keyway lies on the throw axis (A24 end view); panel maximum 3 mm ("3 Maxi" on the K drawing), ours 2.0. (6) The 16 THT LEDs stay (coded parts, MIL-STD-1472 dome visibility); their 32 joints get a bead of neutral-cure silicone (DOWSIL 3145 clear, MIL-A-46146 group II) on the underside; they are the only plated component holes left on the face. (7) Sounder: BZ1 leaves the face for a Floyd Bell MC-09-530-Q, IP68, 5 to 30 V DC, 85 dB(A) at 5 V at 61 cm, 1-1/8 in hole with its 61663 bezel gasket, about 34 mm deep behind the panel plus 11 mm of tabs, at (-180, -100) on the west end where 45 mm of depth is free (the battery module fills the east end under the panel); two flying leads to solder lands. An underside piezo behind 2 mm FR-4 would lose about 34 dB by the mass law. (8) Connectors: `J_PANEL` becomes the SMD 2x10 box header (LCSC C54803514) at (203, 75) with its rows along Y, inside the bearing ring; `J_EPD` the SMD 1x8 header (C41417365) at (100, 100) on the underside; the MAIN and PI leads land on two solder lands each (`J_MAINSW`, `J_PIJ2`; no SMD JST XH without a peg hole exists in the library, and the lead unplugs at PCB-A and at the Pi instead). 32 face holes gone, no pin tip on the face. (9) Vias: the gerbers tent both faces; the fabrication option becomes "plugged" (JLCPCB plugs holes up to 0.5 mm; ours are 0.3 and 0.4; epoxy filled and capped if the form offers it); every via drill at least 0.3 (the 2-layer floor is now in `escape.py`); no via in any seal band. (10) Frame joint: a die-cut ring of PORON 4701-30 on its PET carrier, 0.53 mm (the thinnest unsupported grade is 0.79 mm), on the frame's bearing ring with 16 holes at 3.6, adhesive side to the frame so it stays with the frame at every panel removal; compressed about 0.4 mm, so the Z closure spare of 32.30 becomes about 1.5 mm nominal and 0.5 mm at the top of the float window. M3 x 10 A2 pan heads (RS PRO 528-744) with an internal-tooth star washer under the head on the 8.0 mm underside ring, 0.4 N m, Loctite 243; the face side of the ring is under solder mask, a flat gasket seat with no bare ENIG under a wet gasket. Bond path: frame, insert, screw, star washer, ring. No M3 bonded sealing washer is made (the smallest documented bore is 4.7 mm), so the PORON ring is the seal at the screws and the washer the bond. (11) Case walls, same class: an NBR O-ring 6.5 x 1.0 under the outside hex of each Amphenol Connex 132170 (its 5.80 mm panel-side thread leaves room for panel, ring and nut); Glenair 930-001S06 and 930-001S07 silicone flange gaskets under the D38999/20 shell 13 and the 233-370 shell 15 (their hole patterns match exactly); M4 bonded washers under the plate screws. The hose test decides whether an end-wall plate like 32.29's is needed; the holes then sit under its gasket. (12) Lid: no foam; the lid cavity is 46.1 mm deep, the face 8.8 mm below the rim and the tallest item (APEM lever) 14.75 mm above its bushing, so R17 closes by the numbers and by the clay-pellet check below. Nameplate: outdoor polyester label (3M 7871EC) for the serial data matrix.

**Generators.** `gen_footprints_panel.py`: the switch footprints put their lead lands on the underside as SMD pads, carry the keyway notch or the D outline on Edge.Cuts over the drilled hole (the fab routes the notch after the drill; JLCPCB's minimum non-plated slot is 1.0 mm and it rounds the corners), and lose the face silk ring under the gasket; new `PanelSounder`, `FrameScrew_M3_GND` (8.0 mm ring, face masked) and `LeadLands_1x02`. `gen_pcb_c.py`: the five seal rule areas (display band without copper, lens band and gasket band copper-free on the face and via-free and track-free on the back, since Freerouting ran a track 0.4 mm from the panel edge when the back band allowed it), the die-cut outlines on User.2 (gasket ring, both tape frames, 16 holes) and the lenses on User.3, exported as `pcb-c-display-seals.dxf` for the cutter and the lens supplier. `gen_pcb_c3.py`: panel-mount parts placed by their hole centre. `check_pcb_c.py`: no plated component hole on the face but H1 to H16 and D1 to D16, switch lands SMD on the back, hole centres on their sites within 0.01 mm, the keyway reach 4.35 and width 2.70, the D flat 5.8, the bands present and via-free, via drills 0.3 to 0.5, tenting on both faces, every footprint inside the outline (the J_PANEL lesson), the four connectors flipped SMD parts, the User.2 count. `finish_c5.sh` blocks on the tenting token and exports the DXF; `make_handoff.py` writes the plugging and the notch into ORDER-NOTES; `silk_fix_all.py` loses the ring key; `gen_pcb_cring.py` is marked retired. Sourcing: `docs/respin-research-seal-2026-09-04.md` with 40 sheets in `vendor/seals/`.

**Verification owed before any claim.** Bench, on the built panel in its frame before the stack goes in: flood (the frame window filled with dyed water to 8 mm for 30 min, lid open, white paper under the panel, UV torch on the underside); hose (garden jet from 1 m at every angle for 5 min, then a pressure sprayer on each switch, both lens edges and the frame edge); rain (shower rose, 30 min); dust (talc, cold air 5 min, vacuum, torch on the underside). After each stage all lamps, every switch, one e-paper refresh, touch, and a 24 h look for fog behind both lenses. Reference methods MIL-STD-810 506 (rain) and 510 (dust) and IEC 60529 IPX7 and IP6X, adapted to one bench; the record goes here. Lid clearance: clay pellets on the lens corners, the window lens, each lever tip and the boot, close and latch, measure. Closed case: 30 min bath, lid closed, dry inside. Also owed: a peel test of 5915 on the printed glass border and on the black mask.

**Result (4 Sep, night).** C5 gate ALL PASS, pre-route DRC clean, one Freerouting attempt (45 passes, 61 minutes; a first pass had put two tracks inside the D hole's edge clearance because Freerouting ignores Edge.Cuts inside a footprint, which the footprints now cover with a keep-out zone past the routed outline; a second pass exposed the clean-up cutting a pad off a locked escape stub the router had branched from, also fixed): 0 hard, 0 unrouted, 272 vias, `check_pcb_c.py` ALL PASS on the finished board, both faces tented, 2507 entities in the seals DXF. Deliverable `meshsat-pcb-c-revA-C5` (15 items), order folder `PCB-C-DISPLAY-C5/`, C4 and R1 order folders under `superseded/`.

**Cart.** Line Y20 (C4) is rebuilt from `PCB-C-DISPLAY-C5/` with the via option "plugged" and fewer through-hole rows, line Y21 (R1) is deleted, the C4 and R1 order folders move under `order/superseded/`; nothing is edited until the owner declares the set final.

### 32.35 The compute-module kit: CM5 carrier, USB on the board, radios on native buses, three-module option (owner request 4 Sep 2026, night; plan approved the same night)

**Request.** With the set "far from final", the owner asked for an investigation of a Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 on a carrier of our own, so that the module's USB is exposed on our PCB instead of on sockets and plugs, with peripherals moved to native interfaces where their makers document one (a UART GNSS, the T-Call's own USB pins, and so on); and of a three-module carrier for customers who want redundancy (k3s or Docker Swarm), with CubeOS or only its HAL. Five read-only explorations answered from the makers' documents and both software repositories; the figures and sources are in `docs/respin-research-cm5-2026-09-04.md` and the sheets in `vendor/cm5`, `gnss`, `lte`, `lora`, `zigbee`, `audio` and `cluster`.

**Assessment.** Yes on both counts, with one limit. Today nine USB connectors, seven cables and sixteen mating pairs sit between the Pi 5 and its devices, the Pi's own power plug among them, and the V1 kits showed USB as the field weak point (the 600 mA cap, hub power, wedged dongles, moving ttyACM paths, cables). A single-CM5 carrier removes every plug and cable on the compute side, the 40-pin ribbon and the microSD, gives -20 to +85 C, eMMC and 1.5 times the MTBF, and its routing class (90 and 100 ohm pairs on JLCPCB's four-layer stack) is what A19 and B12 already do. GNSS (I2C plus PPS), LoRa (SPI with the Linux Meshtastic daemon), ZigBee (UART), APRS audio (an I2S codec) and WiFi/BT (on-module, certified antenna) leave USB by their makers' documents. The limit: the SDR stays a USB plug, the LTE modem stays USB on socket pins (a UART-only modem loses its data bearer), and the on-module WiFi is 1x1 where the dongle was 2x2. The three-module carrier is a product variant, not the base kit: about EUR 650 in modules, a Gigabit switch, a supervisor, three converters, forced air and a hardware-owner election, protecting against a compute failure only; the HAL is the right piece of CubeOS to reuse on its own inside a MeshSat cluster stack.

**Design (approved).** (1) PCB-B **B13**: the CM5 (8 GB wireless, 64 GB eMMC) on two Amphenol 10164227-1004A1RLF (4.0 mm stack), powered from the `J_5V_PI` rail without a plug, `PMIC_Enable` and `PWR_Button` on the LTC2954 lines, `nRPIBOOT` and the dedicated USB 2.0 pair on a USB-C for eMMC flashing only, RTC battery, fan on `Fan_PWM` through the IO board's gate, ESD arrays on every external pair; the USB2517I hub moves from A19 to B13 on a USB 2.0 pair of the module with channels for the SDR receptacle (the one plug that stays), an LTE mini PCIe socket (Quectel EG25-G recommended, USB on socket pins), the wall host port over the ribbon, two spares; GNSS u-blox NEO-M9N on I2C with TIMEPULSE, LoRa SX1262 module on SPI, ZigBee EFR32MG21 NCP module on a UART, the RockBLOCK site as today, the Touch Display 2 on MIPI1 through an FH12-22S FPC, `J_PANEL` and the e-paper SPI as today, the module's WiFi/BT on the certified antenna kit; the T-Call, XIAO, T-Beam, ZigBee dongle, GPS puck and WiFi dongle leave. (2) **A20**: the hub and its four dongle channels leave, the wall channel is fed from B13, `J_AB1` grows to 2x8 to carry I2S. (3) **D6**: the STM32 AIOC core becomes a WM8960 codec on I2S plus I2C with PTT on a GPIO line. (4) The cluster variant on the same outline: three CM5 sites, a Microchip KSZ9897 switch (MDI to MDI through 0.1 uF, magnetics on the uplink only), a supervisor MCU electing one hardware owner, every muxed radio moving together (TMUX1308 and TS3USB221), PPS fanned out, the display on node 1, three M.2 2242 sites unpopulated unless k3s is chosen, Docker Swarm with three managers on eMMC, the HAL lifted from CubeOS into a `meshsat-cluster` stack with a supervisor agent and a capability-to-node registry. Not in the design: muxed DSI, a plug-less SDR, triplicated radios, CubeOS whole. Order: B13, A20, D6, then the cluster carrier after B13 is proven, all Rev A. Issues: MESHSAT-795 (B13), MESHSAT-796 (cluster).

**Open at approval, carried as recommendations:** the LTE module (mini PCIe EG25-G recommended over a soldered A7670E), the CM5 variant (wireless with the certified antenna recommended), the cluster base (Swarm on eMMC recommended over k3s with NVMe), and the sequencing above.

**Owner ruling 5 Sep 2026 00:05:** option 2, the receptacles on our own board, proceeds; the three-module carrier waits until B13 is proven. Execution notes (5 Sep 00:00 to 00:40, commits 56ca018 and 91e5d59):

- *Parts and deltas against the plan text.* ZigBee is the Ebyte E72-2G4M20S1E (CC2652P, the Koenkk CC1352P2_CC2652P_other coordinator build, ZNP as the bridge speaks it): the E180-ZG120B in the plan is an EFR32MG1 (Series 1), not an MG21. The display sits on MIPI0 with its control I2C on the module's dedicated SDA0/SCL0 pins, which frees GPIO0/1 for UART1 (ZigBee); UART2 (GPIO4/5) is the RockBLOCK, UART0 (14/15) the console header; PWM0 on 12/13; SPI0 CE0 the e-paper and CE1 the LoRa module; I2S on 18 to 21; LoRa BUSY, DIO1, NRST and the GNSS pulse on 23, 24, 26, 22; the five RockBLOCK lines, both DCF77 lines, the radio resets and boot pins and the WiFi/BT disables sit on two PCA9555 (U20 0x20, U21 0x25). ### 32.36 Finding: the SOT-23 N-channel FETs on A19 and B12 are pinned wrong (found 4 Sep 2026 late evening while writing the B13 generator, written 5 Sep 00:01; fixes ride with A20 and B13)

**What was checked.** KiCad's `Transistor_FET:2N7000` symbol is numbered for the TO-92 part (1 = S, 2 = G, 3 = D); its `2N7002` symbol for the SOT-23 part (1 = G, 2 = S, 3 = D). The four generators were read against those numbers.

**Findings.** (1) A19 `Q5` (the Pi KILL stage, `gen_sch_a.py` line 190) uses the 2N7002 symbol with `{"1": PI_KILL, "2": KILL, "3": GND}`: gate right, source and drain swapped. With the source on `KILL` (100k to CELL+) and the drain on ground, the body diode conducts from KILL to ground whenever the FET is off, so `KILL` sits near 0.6 V and the LTC2954 reads it low from power-up: the kit would switch itself off after the kill delay. (2) B12 `Q1` (the RockBLOCK OnOff buffer, `gen_sch_b.py` line 203) uses the 2N7000 symbol on the SOT-23 land with `{"1": GND, "2": Q1_G, "3": RB_ONOFF}`: right by the symbol's pin functions, wrong on the land, where pad 1 is the gate. The gate is grounded and the 9603 OnOff line is never pulled. (3) C5 (`nfet()` helper, gate source drain on pads 1 2 3) and D5 `Q3` are right.

**Closure.** B13 carries an `nfet(ref, gate, source, drain)` helper on the 2N7002 symbol with a comment that the 2N7000 symbol must never be put on a SOT-23 land; `Q1` is right there. A19's `Q5` is corrected in the A20 respin (its schematic changes anyway: the hub leaves and `J_AB1` grows). The A19 deliverable in `release/revA/boards/` keeps the defect until A20 replaces it; the cart is unpaid and the set is not final (owner, 4 Sep evening), so nothing wrong is ordered. Added to the review method of CLAUDE.md section 7: every transistor's pad map is read against the symbol's pin numbers and the package's pin order.

### 32.38 D7: PCB-D fitted to the DMR858M V1.0 board as delivered, the module owned by the Compute Module (owner review and ruling 5 Sep 2026 06:30, MESHSAT-804)

**What the owner's board is.** The two NiceRF DMR858M ordered on 31 Aug (arrival about 15 Sep) are the V1.0 board that NiceRF's V1.2 datasheet (July 2026, `vendor/dmr858/`) draws on its page 10: heatsink on the front, own SMA jack and USB-C port, a PTT button, a 16-position channel knob and a DIP switch (NORMAL) on the back, two rows of twelve castellated pads. D6 was drawn from that page, so the socket geometry (38.69 x 58.31, 24 pads at 2.54 mm, the two 3.00 mm holes, 19.5 mm tall with the heatsink) matched. The pin table: 1 VCC 3.7 to 8.5 V, 2/4/15/17 GND, 3 CS, 5 PTT, 6 LINE_OUT (0.2 to 460 mV, 130 typical), 7 to 10 the channel code 8/4/2/1 as outputs of the knob, 11/12 OUTP/OUTN (8 ohm 2 W speaker), 13/14 MIC-/MIC+ (bias inside, the silk says MC+/MC-), 16 SPKEN as the receive indication output, 18/19 TXD/RXD the control UART (command set 0x01 to 0x28: channel, power, mic gain), 21/22 HST_TX/HST_RX the upgrade UART, 20/23/24 NC. Currents at 8 V: receive under 165 mA, transmit 900 mA digital and 1700 mA analog at 5 W. Modulation sensitivity 4 to 10 mV.

**What D6 had wrong, and the D7 fix.** (1) SPKEN was driven from the PCA9536 as an output; it is the module's carrier detect: D7 reads it on an expander input through 1k (`R42`), with the 100k pull-down kept, as Direwolf's DCD. (2) The channel pins were tied to solder jumpers as if they were inputs; they are the knob's outputs: the jumpers are gone, the four bits go into expander inputs through 1k (`R43` to `R46`) for read-back. (3) The control UART reached only a bench header, so the Compute Module could not set channel, power or mic gain: D7 carries an NXP SC16IS740 I2C-to-UART bridge `U8` at 0x48 (TSSOP16, A1 = A0 = VDD, I2C mode, CTS low, RESET pulled up by `R47`, clocked by the codec's 24 MHz oscillator on XTAL1, the 100 ohm series pair `R8`/`R9` into the module's RXD/TXD); the Linux `sc16is7xx` driver gives it a tty. The bench header `J_UART1` is gone: the module's own USB-C with its bridge chip is NiceRF's PC-tool path, and the upgrade UART stays unused. (4) The microphone drive was drawn from the older DMR858 sheet's 0.1 to 1.6 Vpp: with the V1.2 sensitivity of 4 to 10 mV, the codec's headphone output divided by four (about 240 mV rms at full scale) sat about 30 dB high; D7 divides by 48 (`R2` 47k, `R4` 1k, about 20 mV rms at full scale) into the module's biased MIC+ through the 4.7 uF. (5) The PCA9536 (0x41) becomes a PCA9555 `U7` at 0x26 (A2 A1 A0 = 1 1 0): P0.0 PTT, P0.1 PTT2 spare, P0.2 status LED, P0.3 CS control (`R48` 1k into the CS pin, `R36` 10k pull-up now on +3V3_AB, low = sleep after 3 s), P0.4 carrier detect, P0.5 to P1.0 the channel code; 0x41 is freed in the I2C map, 0x26 and 0x48 are added. The LINE_OUT path into the codec, the boost (7.58 V typical, under 7.9 V worst case against the 8.5 V maximum, 2 A against the 1.7 A analog 5 W case), the PTT stages with the EMCON inhibit and the TR mirror, the harness and the codec are unchanged; A20, B14 and `check_contracts.py` are untouched.

**Height.** The module sits 11 mm above D7 on its sockets (8.5 mm socket plus 2.5 mm header) with its back-side parts in that gap and the heatsink up: with the 35 mm spacers the heatsink top lands about 49.7 mm above the cavity floor against B14's underside at 51.6. Ruling: 38 mm spacers between A20 and B14 (B14 at Z 54.6, its top at 56.2), about 5 mm over the heatsink, the rods and the room under the panel take it; no board change. What is unreachable in the stack (knob, DIP, PTT button, USB-C) is set on the bench before the module is plugged in.

**Not on D7 by design.** No SMA (the module's own jack goes by a short pigtail to A20's UHF jack), no USB-UART (the module has one behind its USB-C), no speaker driver (OUTP/OUTN unused, LINE_OUT feeds the codec), the module's PTT button in parallel with the PTT transistor is harmless. The bench plan of MESHSAT-748 for 15 Sep stands: AIOC as codec, a USB-UART dongle, 8 V from the UPS, Direwolf, the module's USB-C for the PC tool, before any carrier exists.


**Result (5 Sep 2026 13:52 on the VM):** D7 routed clean at the second run (the first left three opens because the F.Cu pads were not tied to the B.Cu pours; `prefanout.py` on V8 and VIN_CELL and a 0.8 mm CELL class closed them): 0 hard, 0 unrouted, 90 router vias, deliverable `meshsat-pcb-d-revA-D7` (35 BOM lines), retitled to D7 at 16:15; `check_contracts.py` ALL CONTRACTS PASS. The DRC report carries one `zones_intersect` note from the V8 bands at equal priority, which the generator now avoids (distinct priorities) for the next regeneration.

**32.38 (b), 5 Sep 2026 20:50, DMR data over the module (owner question, answered from the vendor sheet):** the DMR858M V1.2 sheet (`v2/vendor/dmr858/dmr858m-v1.2.pdf`, section on the serial protocol, packet 0x68 ... 0x10) lists command 0x07 "SMS mode setting and sending", 0x11 "read received data", 0x10 "output of the received call type and number", 0x09 "emergency alarm", 0x18 contacts, 0x19 encryption; page 3 states SMS sending with a transparent pass-through mode. So DMR short data (position and text, the "DMR APRS" path through Brandmeister's SMS gateway, or kit to kit) is host software over the SC16IS740 bridge of D7; the module has no GPS, the Pi supplies the fix. The byte layout of the SMS packets is in a separate NiceRF serial-protocol document that is not in the vendor folder yet: needed before the bridge code, not before the order.

### 32.39 Finding: the net-class patterns never matched the labelled nets on any board (gateway session, 5 Sep 2026 13:00; fixed in the generators the same minute, A21 owed)

KiCad writes a root-sheet label's net as `/NAME` in the board file, and its net-class pattern matcher does not strip the slash. Every generator's `PATTERNS` list (`gen_pcb_a3.py` to `gen_pcb_e3.py`) was written without it, so only the power-symbol nets (GND, +3V3, +5V) ever left the Default class. Evidence read from the committed boards: on B13 `/USB_LTE_N` is 0.25 mm wide (the USB class says 0.20), on A20 `/CELL+` is 0.25 mm where the BANK class says 1.0 and `/+5V_PI` is 0.25 mm where the RAIL class says 2.0. CELL+ and CELL_N are carried anyway by the hand-laid bars and pours of `fix_a19_node.py` and the outer pours, and `/+5V_M1` sits on its In2 plane, but **`/+5V_PI` on A20 has no bar and no zone**: the module's rail (2.5 A design point, plus the WiFi card's 2.0 A worst case since the 06:00 ruling) runs on 0.25 mm router tracks. `escape.py` had compensated for its own clearance (it matches both forms since 4 Sep), which is why the defect stayed invisible.

Fix (commit 16b0166): every generator emits each label pattern in both forms, `PATTERNS += [("/" + p, c) ...]`, and `check_pcb_b.py` fails when a label pattern matches nothing in either form. Consequences: B14 was relaunched on the fix before its lane was routed; the B13, C5, D6, E4 deliverables in the order set were routed with their differential and power nets in the Default class (0.25 mm; the pair gap and impedance of the USB and DSI pairs are the Default 0.2 mm gap, not the 0.15 of the USB class), which the next regeneration of each corrects; **A21 is owed before any order** so the Pi rail routes in the RAIL class. Recorded as an order-gate item on MESHSAT-795. The same session pointed out the 7628 numbers the record claims for the pairs were therefore never what got routed; the corrected boards make the record true.

**A21, what the class widths alone could not do (5 Sep 2026 14:15 to 15:10, runs 6 to 13 on the VM).** Applying the classes as written (RAIL 2.0 mm, BANK 1.0) left 20 connections open; at 1.0 and 0.6 mm six stayed open, every one at pin 5 of U22, U23 and U24: the TPS61288L's VOUT pin is a 1.25 x 0.40 mm pad with pad 4 and pad 6 0.25 mm away, so no track wider than about 0.5 mm can leave it, and the escape scheme had given each rail one 0.2 mm stub and one 0.45/0.25 via as its whole current path out of the converter. The rail and boost-input currents therefore do not travel in router tracks at all on A21 (`gen_pcb_a3.py`, KiCad frame; the converters U22/U23/U24 sit at x 2.1/34.1/66.1, y 130, the inductors L2/L3/L4 north of them with pad 1 at y 111.5 to 120.5, the blade fuses at y 154.3 to 157.7):

- **Top-side output islands** (`island()`): per converter a 0.5 mm neck over the east end of pad 5 (between pad 6 and the package edge) that widens east of the escape vias into a 14 x 19 mm F.Cu pour over the output capacitor group (full pad connection, 0.15 mm clearance, priority 3), so the VOUT pad, the six output capacitors and the escape via sit in one piece of copper. **Stitch vias** (`stitch()`): six locked 0.8/0.4 vias per island, M1 into the In2 plane south of C70, M2 and PI into the taps of their bottom bands.
- **Bottom bands** (`BANDS`, B.Cu): both rail collectors run north of the inductor row, side by side and parallel (M2 at y 109.5 to 112.8 from x 10 to 51.5, PI at 103.5 to 106.8 from x 25 to 79.5), each with a tap down the east side of its output capacitors to the stitch vias (M2 at x 47.5 to 51.5, PI at 70.5 to 79.5) and a 6 mm riser to its VH pin (M2 at x 10 to 16, PI at x 25 to 31, to y 63.5). Runs 8 and 9 had put the collectors south of the inductors, where every one was cut by a north-south band of another net on the same layer; run 12 put the PI corridor at y 105.5 to 108.8 and R18 pin 2 (the LED rail, at (25.4, 107.6)) stayed open under the riser's keep-out. Same-net bands overlap only at distinct priorities (`check_zone_nets.py`).
- **Boost feeds** (`BOOST`): the Pi converter draws up to 9.5 A at a 3.0 V node and JLC's 4-layer stack has 0.5 oz inner copper (a 6 mm In2 column alone is good for about 3 A at 10 K), so each feed is an In2 column from the blade fuse's BOOST pad (pin 2, x 5/30/55, plated through, so the column starts in the pad itself) north to the inductor row, a B.Cu column of the same width in parallel on both sides of the CELL+ node bar (fuse pad to the bar, bar to the inductor jog), and under the bar itself (y 148.5 to 152, where only inner layers are free) a 19 mm foot on In2 and another on In1, spanning the gap between the CELL+ pad rings of the neighbouring fuses. Locked 0.8/0.4 vias tie the layers at both ends of the bar (four north, two south) and six vias in a top-side tap island over the south end of each inductor's pad 1 bring the current up to the inductor. Run 9's B.Cu feed bands had been centred on the fuses' CELL+ pads (pin 1) and were cut by the node bar and by the M2 collector; the boost 1 column starts 0.5 mm east of U22's BST1 escape via after run 10 left that net open with the keep-out edge touching the via; the bootstrap capacitors C38, C71 and C84 moved from the compensation row (13 mm west of each converter, across the feed column) to right under their converters after runs 10 and 14 left BST1 and BST2 open.
- **Track keep-outs and spines**: every collector, riser, column, foot and jog carries a rule area on its layer that forbids tracks and permits vias. The output islands and inductor taps carry none: a keep-out over them hid their capacitor pads from the router, which could place no via inside it and thrashed for 14 minutes (run 20); they go to the router as DSN planes instead, and since Freerouting keeps no clearance from a plane outline (run 21: a BST3 track along U24's island edge made the fill retreat and cut the neck off the body), each island neck and each inductor tap carries a locked copper spine (`spine()`, 0.4 mm from pad 5 through the neck into the body, 0.8 mm from the inductor pad through the middle via column) that the router treats as a fixed obstacle (the two rail taps and the In1 spare feet carry none: the taps sit in the capacitor columns whose GND vias need the room, and run 13 left BOOST_EN open when it could not via past the M2 tap; the In1 feet are best-effort parallel copper and are not gated) (`track_keepout()`; KiCad exports it as a `wire_keepout`), so the router crosses a band on another layer and cannot slice it; `escape.py` and `prefanout.py` ignore a rule area that permits vias. Two router facts learnt on the way: exporting the bands as DSN planes (run 8) made the router end tracks at band edges the fill never reached, so `route_one.sh` strips every zone from the DSN again; and Freerouting places no via of its own inside a wire keep-out, so a pad under a band whose net must leave on an inner layer needs the band moved or a pre-placed via (R18, BST1).
- **The converters' enable line by hand**: `bus_a21.py` runs after the escapes and lays BOOST_EN as a locked 0.25 mm In1 bus south of the converter row joining the three pin-6 escape vias, on the first row it finds clear of foreign vias and through pads; runs 13 and 17 had left that link open because between U23 and U24 every layer but In1 is walled by the boost 3 feed and Freerouting did not find the In1 path.
- **Classes**: RAIL is the link width only, 0.5 mm (via 1.0/0.5); BANK 0.6 (CELL+ and MEZZ_CELL; CELL_N's gauge link is a sense connection in PWR, the return bar carries its current), BOOST 0.8; `prefanout.py` locks its pad-to-pour ties like the escapes. `check_pcb_a.py` reads the routed widths of the unlocked tracks over 0.7 mm against those floors, and on a filled board it also requires every rail band, boost column, island and inductor tap to be one piece over at least half its outline, every M2 and PI stitch via to sit in a filled rail band, every feed stitch via in a filled In2 feed and a filled B.Cu feed, and the pieces of one rail or feed to touch; `finish_a21.sh` refills, runs that gate, and refuses to finish or commit with an open connection, a hard violation or a FAIL (`finish_b14.sh` and the B14 chain refuse an open board the same way since 15:00).

**Result (5 Sep 2026 16:11, run 23 of A21):** routed clean on the VM in three attempts of 40, 55 and 70 passes (identical results), 0 hard violations, 0 unrouted, 132 router vias on top of the locked copper (18 island stitch vias, 18 inductor tap vias, 18 feed stitch vias, the enable bus, six spines, 148 escapes, 80 fanout ties); the routed-board gate passes every band, island, tap and column (the three In2 columns are two pieces each, split by their own foot, and every piece touches it); `check_contracts.py` ALL CONTRACTS PASS; deliverable `meshsat-pcb-a-revA-A21`. The DRC's 22 dangling vias and 9 dangling tracks are the stitch vias, spines and bus ends that terminate in zone fills, which KiCad counts as dangling; none of the hard types remain. Runs 6 to 22 are logged under `~/render3d/logs-20260905/a21-vm-try*.log` on the VM.

### 32.40 Rulings, 5 Sep 2026 evening (owner, one by one at 16:45 to 17:00)

1. **The B14 pair mismatch is closed by the tool, not by hand or by a review round** (decision 1, 16:45): `tools/meander.py` extended to segments of any angle with a sliding free window, `run_meander_b14.sh`; result in 32.37 (TX and RX 0.00 mm, CLK 0.25 mm, DRC unchanged).
2. **A differential pair over 1 mm of intra-pair mismatch is a hard gate** (decision 2, 17:00): `pair_match.sh` runs in the B finish, meanders every short leg by its mismatch (three rounds, the board kept only when the DRC hard count and the open count do not rise), and `finish_b14.sh` refuses to finish and commit while a pair stays over 1 mm. **No human look when it stops:** the finish writes an audit image per pair (`pair_audit.py`, the two legs and every copper item of the region per layer) and the session reads it, traces the cause and iterates until the gate passes. The same posture applies to any future pair on any board.
3. **In1 is a solid ground plane** (decision 3, 17:08). The audit image of the length-matched B14 lane showed each PCIe leg running 40 to 90 mm on In1 (the ground plane) and 60 to 115 mm on In2 (the 5 V plane), in slots of those planes, with the legs of a pair side by side for only 19 to 41 percent of their length (up to 34 mm apart): matched edges, but no defined impedance and no coupling, because the chains had stripped every plane from the router's view since A17 and let it use In1 as a signal layer. Ruled: a board-wide rule area on In1 that forbids tracks and permits vias (`gen_pcb_b3.py`), so the router keeps to F.Cu, In2 and B.Cu, the normal use of a 4-layer stack, and every inner track has the solid ground next to it (the 0.2 mm PCIe tracks near 50 ohm single-ended); the pair gate meanders the legs again after the rerun. B14 reruns now; A21 keeps its In1 tracks (enable bus, spare feet) until its next regeneration, when the same rule applies; every board gets the rule at its next regeneration. Options declined: hand-laid coupled pairs on the top layer (hours, uncertain today) and accepting the lane for Rev A with a bench test.
4. **The kit moves to the Peli 1450** (19:05, after the case study of 32.41): "ok go with the 1450". The boards that do not depend on the case are not resized (A21, B14, D7, E4, E5 stay as released; asked whether all boards must be reshaped, the owner ruled "only the boards that need resizing get resized"), the panel is respun as C6 on the 1450PF, the wall templates, the battery cradle, the record's case numbers, the scene and the renders follow.
5. **The face is an aluminium plate with a backer board** (19:30): asked whether the PCB face is a good idea for a prototype, the answer was that it works on the bench but flexes under a hand and puts that flex into the switch and LED joints and the gasket, "the aluminium plate with a backer board is the safer face for anything that leaves the bench"; the owner ruled "V2 goes with this plan", on the condition that everything is proven to fit first (the numbers are the context block of the plan of 19:40 and 32.42). Supersedes the one-board face of 32.34 where that construction existed only because the PCB was the face; the seals of 32.34 stay as parts.
6. **B goes to six layers (B15)** so that decision 3 can be met: on four layers a board-wide In1 keep-out and a keep-out with a window around the CM5 receptacles both left the router thrashing (17:08 and 17:45 runs, 93 opens at 8 passes in the diagnostic of 18:47); the CM5 breakout needs two inner signal layers, so B15 takes the JLC six-layer stack with solid ground on In1 and the 5 V plane on In4. A21 keeps its four layers until its next regeneration.
7. **Renders with rulers** (19:05): at least 24 images from every corner with all antennas, holes and cables, each with a ruler for scale.
8. **Battery module: one row of twelve upright cells along the west end wall** (19:55, asked as a multiple choice after the 1450's interior was drawn from the 1451-931 DXF): the flat four-by-three block of 32.22 needs an 81 mm strip and the 1450 gives 44 mm beside the stack and 38 mm at the ends (the front wall carries the valve body and the handle inside), so the module becomes a 229 x 24 x 70 mm enclosure standing on the floor along the west end wall, one BMS, 42 Ah unchanged, outside the lift-out path; the end-wall antenna bulkheads move from Z 55 to Z 88 on both walls (above the row, below the frame skirt at 100), where WiFi P2P B already sat at 90. Declined: two rows of six on two walls (two enclosures on a harness), one row of eight (28 Ah).

   First run on the rule (17:08 to 17:45): with In1 closed over the whole board the three router attempts thrashed for 36 minutes without writing a session and were killed. Cause traced: the two 0.4 mm receptacles fan 200 pins out through vias at the pad tips with alternating 0.3 and 1.0 mm escape depths, a scheme that needs both inner layers under the module. The rule area is therefore four bands that leave a window 8 mm around the receptacles open on In1 (`gen_pcb_b3.py`, 17:45): the ground is solid everywhere but under the module, and the PCIe pairs leave the window on In2 or B.Cu.

### 32.43 The Freerouting quality programme (6 Sep 2026 00:15, owner rulings of 5 Sep 23:55 and 6 Sep 00:01)

**Why.** The evening of 5 Sep showed the plumbing around Freerouting certifying instead of catching (32.42 (b), CLAUDE.md section 8): a generator that failed without a traceback was filtered out of a chain log, a stub router without numpy crashed silently in every finish since the move to the VM, three route attempts thrashed for 75 minutes and left nothing to look at, and the multi-thread optimiser knotted two nets into 39 micro-fragment violations. `tools/routeflow.py` (methodology in `v2/docs/routeflow-methodology.md`, audited from the territory-grounder, logos, finops-agora and claude-gateway repositories) now supervises every route fail-closed with an append-only journal and a bounded remedy table. The owner asked how confident that makes us and whether routeflow can bring Freerouting to TopoR's level; the honest answer is that routeflow proved reliability and measured nothing about routing quality, so a measured programme was approved (plan of 6 Sep 2026): a capability probe of the router's knobs, a router-agnostic metrics instrument and a baseline, an experiment loop over the knobs and the pre-route tools, post-route quality passes of our own, a gated A/B of Freerouting 2.4.1, and targets against our own baseline (owner ruling 23:55: no TopoR install; TopoR's traits define the direction of the metrics, not a number). **Owner ruling 6 Sep 00:01:** the old shell chains were stopped mid-run; every route from now goes through routeflow.

**The instrument** (`tools/route_metrics.py`) measures a board from its `.kicad_pcb` and its kicad-cli DRC JSON, never from a router log: completion with denominators, hard violations by type, vias total and router-added (the locked pre-route copper counted apart), length total and per layer, segments and micro-segments, bends, the longest nets, the per-net detour ratio (routed length over the minimum spanning tree of the net's pads), differential-pair skew for every `_P`/`_N` pair, layer balance, and the run times the caller passes in. `tools/bench_compare.py` grades a run: any hard or open makes it INELIGIBLE (recorded, never ranked), a pair over 1 mm or router vias or length up 5 percent is a REGRESSION, else MET with Q = 0.5 x vias ratio + 0.3 x length ratio + 0.2 x segment ratio (1.0 = the released board, lower is better; time is shown beside Q, never folded in). `tools/bench_baseline.sh` reproduced the released boards exactly (self-check within 1 percent) and wrote `tools/routeflow/bench/baseline.json`; `tools/strip_route.py` turns a released board back into its pre-route board (the locked copper stays) so experiments start without re-running a chain; `tools/fr_probe.sh` is the knob probe.

**Baseline of 5 Sep 2026 (generated from `baseline.json`; the numbers every later claim is measured against):**

| Board | Layers | Nets | Connections | Vias (router) | Vias per net | Length mm | Segments (micro) | Bends | Detour median / p90 | Pairs over 1 mm | Layer balance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A21 | 4 | 117 | 487 | 404 (132) | 3.45 | 10694 | 2051 (68) | 1243 | 1.198 / 1.435 | 1 | 19.86 |
| B14 | 4 | 184 | 720 | 704 (270) | 3.83 | 24675 | 4046 (138) | 2622 | 1.164 / 1.392 | 9 | 12.17 |
| C5 | 2 | 86 | 234 | 330 (272) | 3.84 | 21436 | 2015 (95) | 1417 | 1.266 / 1.451 | 0 | 1.56 |
| D7 | 4 | 61 | 194 | 148 (90) | 2.43 | 3618 | 958 (32) | 620 | 1.186 / 1.584 | 0 | 3.87 |
| E4 | 4 | 44 | 173 | 142 (142) | 3.23 | 3772 | 773 (41) | 444 | 1.222 / 1.392 | 1 | 14.67 |
| E5 | 2 | 14 | 21 | 14 (14) | 1.00 | 112 | 36 (0) | 18 | 1.433 / 1.686 | 0 | 1.13 |

**What the baseline already says.** B14 carries 9 differential pairs over 1 mm of intra-pair skew (the DSI display pairs, 1.7 to 7.8 mm; only the PCIe pairs were matched on 5 Sep) and E4 and A21 one each: the pair matcher must cover every `_P`/`_N` pair, not a list. Layer balance is poor on the four-layer boards (A21 19.9, E4 14.7, B14 12.2: almost nothing on B.Cu), which is the router's preferred-direction and via-cost behaviour and the first thing the experiment loop measures. Median detour is 1.16 to 1.27 with p90 1.39 to 1.58 (E5 is a 14-net block): the routes are not long, they are via-heavy (2.4 to 3.8 vias per net). Targets committed in the plan: Q at or under 0.85 on the dense boards, router vias per net down 25 percent, length down 8 percent, completion 100 percent with 0 hard in one routeflow run with at most one remedy round, route wall time at most twice today's, detour median at or under 1.3 and p90 at or under 2.0, every pair within 1 mm without a manual step.

**Stage 0 result, the capability probe (6 Sep 2026 00:35, `tools/fr_probe.sh`, D7 stripped to its locked copper, Freerouting 1.9.0 on Java 21, one thread, 40 passes; `tools/routeflow/bench/capabilities.json`):** the base run gave 130 vias, 3561 mm, 968 segments in 35 s. `-us global`, `-us hybrid 1:1`, `-is sequential`, `-is random`, `-oit 0.5`, `-mp 10` and `-im` returned byte-identical boards: on a board the router completes, those flags change nothing in 1.9.0. `-inc PWR` changed the result only by leaving the PWR class unrouted (100 vias, 2894 mm), so it is a skip, not a knob. **A rules file passed with `-dr` carrying `(autoroute_settings ... (via_costs 200) ...)` cut the vias to 98 (25 percent fewer) for 4011 mm (13 percent longer) in 84 s:** the via and ripup costs and the per-layer preferred directions in that block are the lever the 1.9.0 router honours, so Stage 2 sweeps them (`tools/fr_rules.py` writes the file, `route_one.sh` passes it as `FR_RULES`) and drops the strategy flags. A jar killed after 20 s with `-im` leaves no session or checkpoint: `NO_SESSION` stays a real failure class.

**Stage 3, first pass (`tools/straighten.py` under `tools/quality_pass.sh`, 6 Sep 00:40, on copies of the released boards):** merging collinear segments and shortcutting corner pairs that collide with nothing (the larger class clearance of the two nets, never under the board minimum, plus 5 um; the board edge counted) at 0 hard and 0 unrouted: A21 2051 to 1918 segments (6.5 percent) and 10693 to 10622 mm; B14 4046 to 3777 (6.6 percent) and 24675 to 24570 mm; D7 958 to 896 (6.5 percent) and 3618 to 3596 mm; vias unchanged (the via pass is next). Three defects were caught by the DRC gate on the way and fixed in the pass, not in the gate: a snap of micro-segments moved a track end laterally and broke a 0.15 mm clearance (removed); junctions were counted over unlocked segments only, so a locked escape stub meeting at a corner was invisible and the corner was cut (now every live segment counts); imported vias sit nanometres off the track ends, so an exact position match missed a via under a corner (now a radius test). The wrapper itself was corrected first: it had accepted an unchanged board when the pass crashed silently; a pass must now leave its own summary line or it counts as failed.

**Stage 3, the via pass (`tools/via_merge.py`, 6 Sep 00:45):** a post-route via remover (a via, a run on one layer, a via back, replaced by a straight segment on the layer both vias share when that is free) found nothing to remove on B14: of 253 unlocked router vias, 21 chains reached another via, 17 of them a locked escape via, 4 were blocked on the shared layer, none qualified. The router's vias mostly land on escape vias or pads, not in removable excursions, so post-route via removal has no room here; via reduction has to come from the router's own via cost (the probe: 25 percent fewer vias at via_costs 200), which is what Stage 2 sweeps. The pass stays available in `quality_pass.sh` (it costs seconds and reports its counters) but is not counted on.

**Stage 4 begun on the owner's instruction (6 Sep 2026 00:52: "upgrade to 2.4.1 now and run the A/B", then "do not wait for them to finish, run from scratch with the latest version and the agentic plumbing"):** Java 25 and Freerouting 2.4.1 (built 3 Sep 2026) installed on the VM beside 1.9.0; `route_one.sh` drives either jar on the identical DSN. Two facts from the first minutes: a `-drc <file>` argument makes 2.4.1 run a DRC of the DSN and exit without routing (no session), so it is not a route-time flag; and 2.4.1's own fanout pre-pass, on by default, escaped 200 of 219 SMD pins of the stripped D7 and raised the router's via count to 106 against 1.9.0's 72 on the same DSN at only 8 passes, so the production runs switch it off (our escapes are already locked in) and the A/B carries an explicit fanout-on variant. 2.4.1 prints a line per pass with the unrouted count and a score, which 1.9.0 never did. The night-1 1.9.0 runs (B15 round 2 mid-route) were stopped at 00:49; night 2 runs B15 and C6 from scratch on 2.4.1 through routeflow, then the five-board A/B, then the S1 sweeps.

**Stage 2 and Stage 4 moved to a rented box (6 Sep 2026 01:20 to 01:45; owner instruction: "study carefully the official documentation for vast.ai instances ... find the BIGGEST CPU instance with the BIGGEST required RAM to support x16 or x32 parallelism and do it there"):** the night-2 queue on the VM was cut to the two production runs (B15 round 2 on 2.4.1 was routing at 01:20 after round 1 left 10 opens at 0 hard; C6 waits behind it), and the A/B and the S1 sweeps went to a vast.ai instance: two EPYC 9654 (384 threads), 503 GB, a verified host in Taiwan at 1.20 dollars per hour (instance 50008668; `tools/routeflow/cloud/`). Routeflow gained `--parallel N`, named locks and a timeout scale (`v2/docs/routeflow-methodology.md` section 8). Twelve experiment files run side by side: the A/B (1.9.0 base and via_costs 200 against 2.4.1 base, via_costs 200 and fanout) on D7, E4, A21, B14, C6 and B15, and the S1 sweep (12 rules-file configurations) on the same six boards, 132 routes in all, 76 at once. The first hour cost a lesson: the headless Java 25 package kills Freerouting 1.9.0 within a second (HeadlessException under Xvfb), so 84 configurations were rerun after the full JRE went in, and a route that dies within a minute is now a tool failure that routeflow reruns, never a measurement. First rows at 01:43: D7 ripup400 MET (router vias 76 against 90, length +0.8 percent); 2.4.1 base leaves 4 of 194 connections open on D7, 5 of 487 on A21 and 1 of 173 on E4 where 1.9.0 completes, so the Stage 4 completion gate is in question for 2.4.1 on the small boards. The table follows from `bench_report.py` when the box is done.

**The B rows of the box were a B14 route in B15's clothes (6 Sep 2026 03:50):** the journal's pre-route hash showed the B15 experiments reading the file the B14 strip had just written (both cbd9c5a3b6d6; the six-layer B15 board hashes c44e9cc27b23), and the two S1 sweeps on the same project directory overwrote each other's configuration directories; every pcb-b-compute row was discarded (39 of 142) and the four B experiments run again in their own directories at 04:14, under a project lock that now refuses a second experiment on a busy directory (methodology section 8). The D7, E4, A21 and C6 rows are unaffected (distinct configuration names, identical pre-route bytes) and are being re-finished under the production finish (stub router, raw counts kept beside the finished ones).

### 32.44 C6 on four layers, the ground plane as a router plane, and the 2.4.1 completion record (6 Sep 2026 04:20 to 05:05)

**Why the two-layer backer could not close.** Every C6 route of the quality programme's box (twelve 1.9.0 configurations and four 2.4.1 ones on the run-3 pre-route board) left 14 to 35 connections open, all in the driver cluster at the foot of the right strip (LED cathodes, expander lines, 3V3): a two-layer board whose GND is routed as wires between 116 footprints in a 52 by 58 mm cluster, with the twenty ribbon lines passing three button bodies on the way. The audit image (`route_audit.py` on the via100 route: 14 opens, one net) shows both layers full in the cluster and clear everywhere else.

**Decision (applied from the ruling of 5 Sep 2026 17:08, "In1 is a solid ground plane on every board from its next regeneration"):** C6 is a four-layer backer: F.Cu and B.Cu as before, In1 a solid GND plane over the whole U, In2 a routing layer; 1.6 mm as the backer already was (`gen_pcb_c.py` sets four copper layers and JLC's four-layer via floor 0.4/0.2; `gen_pcb_c3.py` adds the In1 zone; `check_pcb_c.py` requires four layers and the In1 GND zone; `finish_c6.sh` lets the stub router use In2). The backer sits behind a 3 mm aluminium plate, so nothing of C5's sealed two-layer construction (2.0 mm, plugged vias) applies to it. The pre-route passed its gates at 04:40 (116 footprints, 87 nets, 72 escapes, 25 fanout vias, 0 hard). Cost: a four-layer 344 by 228 mm U at JLC instead of a two-layer one, for five boards.

**The plane in the DSN (route_one.sh `FR_PLANE_NETS`, routeflow `plane_nets` and the `planes` knob).** The B15 DSN listed 258 GND pins for the router, 37 percent of its 703 connections, because every zone is stripped from the DSN before the export (the A17 practice) and In1 is a power-type layer the router may not wire on: the router was drawing GND as wires on the four signal layers. With the In1 GND zone kept in the DSN as a plane, the router connects a GND pin by one via into the plane. Probe running on the box at 04:40 (`s2_b15.json`: 1.9.0 and 2.4.1 with the plane, 1.9.0 with the plane and via_costs 200) against the plain B15 rows; the four-layer C6 runs the same comparison (`ab_c6_4l.json`, with a no-plane control). The KiCad fill and DRC after the route remain the judge: a via the fill cannot reach is an open, and the gate refuses it.

**B15 on 2.4.1 (the production run of the owner's 00:52 instruction):** round 1 (100 passes) 0 hard, 10 opens; round 2 (via_costs 100) open; round 3 (130 passes, via_costs 100) stalled at 49 opens with the same score for passes 22 to 24 and was stopped at 04:22, 73 minutes in, with the outcome already known. The first 1.9.0 routeflow run of 00:20 had come back 0 hard, 1 open. B15 runs on 1.9.0 since 04:25 (`b15_fr19.json`, the same profile with the 1.9.0 jar), and the inner-layer stub router closes a single open. On the box, 2.4.1 base leaves opens where 1.9.0 completes on D7 (4 of 194), E4 (1 of 173) and A21 (3 of 487); the Stage 4 gate is graded by `bench_report.py` from the rows when the box is done.

### 32.45 The Iridium antenna, the GNSS receiver and its antenna (research, 6 Sep 2026 15:50, owner question of 15:35)

**What the renders showed and what it was.** The white disc on the east wall was a stand-in for the Iridium antenna, the dark disc on the west wall a stand-in for the GNSS antenna; the receiver itself is not on a wall: B15 carries a u-blox NEO-M9N (four concurrent constellations, L1 only, I2C to the CM5 with its time pulse on GPIO 22, UART available) whose antenna path is the west-wall SMA (the "GNSS puck" of the early A-board designs was a USB receiver on PCB-A and is retired since B13).

**Iridium (RockBLOCK 9704 SMA, our variant).** Ground Control's data sheet (RB9704-001-JUN26, `vendor/rockblock/`) and its antenna page: the SMA variant takes an external antenna and carries a U.FL GNSS passthrough for a separate GNSS receiver (for a combined Iridium plus GNSS antenna); the approved external antenna is the **Maxtena M1621HCT-P-SMA** helical (Ground Control ACC-HELANT-9704, Maxtena 100-00003-02; `vendor/rockblock/maxtena-m1621hct-p-sma-datasheet.pdf`): 1616 to 1626.5 MHz, 2.8 dBic RHCP, 49 mm high by 19 mm diameter, SMA male, IP67, ground-plane independent, 80 dollars. Installation rules from the same page: axis pointing vertically up, a clear view of the sky, at least 1 m above the ground or any metal that acts as a ground plane, at most 1 m of LMR240 between antenna and modem (0.34 dB/m plus 0.1 dB per connector), outdoor connectors IP66 or better. So it is a helical, not a patch (the record's "Iridium patch" of 32.37 came from the patch variant of the module, which is not ours). On our east wall it screws onto the bulkhead through a right-angle SMA adapter so its axis stands up; standing 49 mm above a socket at Z 88 it clears the base rim (109) by 28 mm and must come off for the lid to close, which is how such kits travel.

**GNSS receiver upgrade (the owner's ask: UART, external antenna, modern, all constellations).** Two candidates from the makers' pages:
- **u-blox NEO-F10N**: L1 and L5 dual-band (L1C/A, L5, E1B/C, E5a, B1C, B2a), GPS, Galileo, BeiDou and QZSS (GLONASS and NavIC are not on its list), UART, time pulse, 12.2 x 16.0 x 2.4 mm, "pin-compatible with previous NEO products", 2.7 to 3.6 V, -40 to +85 C, LNA and SAW filters on board. The same package family as the NEO-M9N on B15, so the site change is small (the data sheet's pin table is still to be filed).
- **Quectel LG290P**: quad-band L1, L2, L5 and E6, all six constellations including GLONASS and NavIC, RTK with fast convergence, UART and I2C, 12.2 x 16 x 2.6 mm, -40 to +85 C, anti-jamming; the technical documents sit behind a login.
Recommendation for the V2 mission (a robust fix and a time pulse for a comms kit, not centimetre surveying): the **NEO-F10N** with the **u-blox ANN-MB1** L1/L5 active antenna (UBX-21005551: 82 x 60 x 22.5 mm, 164 g with its 5 m RG174 cable, SMA plug, magnetic base or M4 screws, IP67, 3.0 to 5.0 V at 15 mA, gain 3.8 dBic L1 and 1.3 dBic L5 plus 29 to 33 dB LNA). If "all constellations" must include GLONASS and NavIC, the LG290P is the pick, at the price of a new site and a login for its documents. Either way the antenna sits on the lid or the case top when deployed with its cable to the west socket. Owner ruling owed on the receiver; nothing changes on B15 until then.

### 32.46 External antennas from the Quectel brochure, the LG290P at Antratek, and the port label of the APRS radio (research, 6 Sep 2026 16:25, owner links of 16:00 and 16:10)

**Sources.** The owner sent Quectel's antenna brochure (December 2025 edition, 117 pages, filed as `vendor/quectel/quectel-antenna-brochure-2025-12.pdf`; the page numbers below are PDF pages) and Antratek's page of the SparkFun LG290P breakout (GPS-26620). Everything below is read from those two documents and the SparkFun and Quectel product pages; nothing is measured, nothing is ordered.

**The nine bulkheads and what fits.** The end-wall jacks are SMA, so an antenna screws on with an SMA male; "terminal mount" in the brochure means exactly that, the other mounts hang on a lead.

|---|---|---|---|
| IRIDIUM (east) | RockBLOCK 9704, 1616 to 1626 MHz | none: the Maxtena M1621HCT-P-SMA of 32.45 stays | the brochure's NTN antenna YETN001L1A (p. 52: GNSS L1, L-band and Iridium on one SMA, passive, 106.15 x 87.21 x 26.5 mm, screw mount, IP67 and IP69K) would feed two receivers from one jack and needs a splitter; the 9704 SMA variant has its own antenna port, so it keeps the approved helical |
| GNSS (west) | the receiver of the ruling below | for the LG290P **YEGD006U1A** (p. 48): 1164 to 1300 and 1525 to 1606 MHz, RHCP, active, 109.28 x 89 x 25.8 mm, adhesive, magnetic and screw mount, SMA male on a 5055 mm RG174 lead, IP68; for the NEO-F10N **YEGB000Q1A** (p. 47): 1164 to 1189 and 1559 to 1606 MHz, RHCP, LNA 17 dB, 62 x 56 x 23 mm, adhesive and magnetic, SMA male on 3000 mm RG174, IP68, IK09 | on the Antratek page: the u-blox ANN-MB2 (GPS-27500, EUR 119.95 ex VAT: 1166 to 1285 and 1535 to 1602 MHz, LNA 31 dB, 5 m RG174, SMA) for the LG290P, the ANN-MB1 of 32.45 for the F10N; a magnetic puck needs a steel seat (Antratek's ground plate GPS-17519, EUR 7.95) because the 1450 is polymer |

| LORA (east) | Wio-SX1262, 868 MHz | **YECT003W1A** again (868 MHz sits inside its 698 to 960 MHz band) | the dedicated 863 to 930 MHz stubby YENT060W1AM (p. 54: dia 9.4 x 34.7 mm, 1.9 dBi, SMA male) lists no IP rating; YENT005W7AM (p. 57: 860 to 870 MHz fiberglass, 600 mm, N male, IP67) for a mast |

Combos: the screw-mount domes (YEMN017AA 5in1, p. 40: two 600 to 960 plus 1400 to 6000 MHz elements, two 1400 to 6000 MHz elements and GNSS L1/L5, dia 103.5 x 42.5 mm, five SMA males on 300 mm leads, IP67 and IP69K) could carry LTE, both WiFi P2P leads and GNSS from one dome, but only fitted permanently to a flat surface; the kit travels closed with its antennas off, so the picks stay one antenna per jack.

**The GNSS receiver, revisited with the owner's own criterion.** The ask was UART, external antenna, modern, "supports all GPS constellations". The NEO-F10N of 32.45 lacks GLONASS and NavIC; the LG290P carries all six. Facts from the SparkFun and Quectel pages of today (ordering code LG290P03AAMD): 12.2 x 16 x 2.6 mm, 0.9 g, 3.15 to 3.45 V at 91 mA (12 uA in backup), three UARTs (9600 to 3,000,000 baud, 460800 by default), I2C and SPI listed as under development on the SparkFun page, 10 Hz by default and 20 Hz at most, an active-antenna feed with a configurable bias, quad-band RTK, PPP-B2b and Galileo HAS, RTKHOLD, NIC anti-jamming, -40 to +85 C. The breakout costs EUR 179.95 ex VAT at Antratek (GPS-26620, in stock) and USD 189.95 at SparkFun; the NEO-F10N breakout EUR 44.95 (GPS-24114). SparkFun's product page links the hardware design manual and the protocol specification (Quectel's own site needs a login). On the board (B16, the next regeneration of PCB-B) either module replaces the NEO-M9N site on the module's UART with the time pulse on GPIO 22; the NEO-M9N has no LCSC code either, so the successor is a bench-fitted part like it. The recommendation moves to the **LG290P**: it is the only one of the two that meets the constellation criterion as stated, and its anti-jamming unit suits a comms kit in a crowded band. The F10N stays the lower-power (about a third of the current) and cheaper choice if GLONASS and NavIC are not required. Owner ruling owed (one question, asked 16:25); render pass 4 shows the puck of the ruled receiver on the west jack.

**The APRS port is VHF, not UHF.** The bulkhead has been called "SMA UHF" since the design brief (section 7, the UV-K5 era, when the handheld could do both bands); the module ordered on 31 Aug 2026 is the DMR858M VHF variant (134 to 174 MHz, MESHSAT-748) and the bridge's spectrum monitor watches 144.7 to 144.9 MHz. The label is corrected in the render scene now (the west-wall port reads VHF); the A21 silk line "SMA -> UHF bulkhead", D7's schematic description of the module, the case template and the documents that carry the old word are a text swap owed with the next touch of each (the GNSS relabel of 5 Sep 2026 is the pattern: strings swapped in the routed board, no regeneration).

**Ruling 6 Sep 2026 16:20 (owner): the GNSS receiver is the Quectel LG290P** ("yes go with the LG290P"), and the two antenna stand-ins of the renders go: both ports are plain SMA bulkheads like the other seven, one for the LG290P's antenna (west wall) and one for the RockBLOCK 9704 (east wall). Consequences: B16 is PCB-B with the LG290P on the NEO-M9N site (UART to the module, time pulse on GPIO 22, active-antenna bias from the module's own pin), after today's 1450 deliverables; the LG290P documents are filed under `vendor/quectel/` (hardware design V1.1, protocol specification V1.1, module specification V1.3, SparkFun's breakout schematic); the fourth render set shows the Maxtena helical on the east jack and the Quectel YEGD006U1A puck on its lead at the west jack in the open views, nothing on the jacks in the closed views (the kit travels with its antennas off).

### 32.47 C6 keeps In1 routable: the keep-out board does not complete, and the case rendered from Peli's drawing (6 Sep 2026 16:55)

**The C6 In1 experiment (`ab_c6_4lk`, pre-route 4e9480f678e9, the four-layer backer with In1 reserved as ground outside the two driver clusters).** Freerouting 1.9.0 plain: 0 hard, 17 open after the route, 7 open after the stub router closed 10; 1.9.0 with 100 passes: 0 hard, 10 open, 5 open after the stub router closed 5 (183 router vias); 2.4.1 stalled at 36 opens on the same board (32.44). The opens lie along the left strip's switch pads and the bottom strip's panel bus, not in one spot: with In1 reserved the strips carry the whole panel bus on three layers and no router closes it. **Decision:** C6 stays as released (03126d3: In1 routable, the GND pour filling In1 around the tracks, 0 hard, 0 open, 240 router vias). The In1 ground-plane ruling of 5 Sep 2026 17:08 was made for the PCIe lanes of PCB-B; the backer carries LED drives, switch contacts, the I2C bus and the panel ribbon, none of them impedance-controlled, so the plane's reason does not apply to it; this is the C6 exception to that ruling, on the same footing as the CM5 window on B15, and it answers the peer audit's "C6 In1, reroute" item of MESHSAT-813 with the numbers above. Rows in `tools/routeflow/bench/results.jsonl`, audit images in the session record.

**The case in the renders (owner, 17:00: "the case you are using in the renders is like a pixelated Super Mario case, add the details properly").** Peli's 1451-931 STEP bodies are envelopes (a slab, a drafted block and a rim ring: 75 and 39 faces), which is what the first four sets showed. The scene now builds the shell from the customer drawing's views and sections (`vendor/peli/1450/1451-931-customer-drawing.dxf` and its PDF): outer 375 x 261 at the bottom drafting to 383 x 269 under the seam flange, the flange ring 411 x 291 x 12 on each half, the lid 45.5 high with a 259 deep top; on the lid the two ladder rails per end at X +-114 and +-156 with rungs at Y +78 and -82, the 85 x 50 R3 label recess at (-59, +77) and the 114 x 18 nameplate recess on its front; two double-throw latches at X +-135 in 43 mm channels with their levers, pivot bands and pins on the lid and the keeper blocks on the flange; padlock protectors split at the seam at X +-176 with the hasp hole; the handle pocket 220 x 78 in the front wall with the U handle on pivots at X +-76, its grip and finger ribs, and the pressure valve at (-16, 62) on the pocket floor; hinge blocks at X +-124 with four knuckles at 22 mm pitch, three lugs and a pin; four feet pads 38 x 23 at (+-132, +-62); three nubs per end wall on each half at Y 0 and +-83.5. Everything is a render of the drawing's forms, not Peli's CAD.

**Finding on the end walls: the 1450's moulded nubs sit on the jack line.** The side view puts three nubs per half on each end wall at Y 0 and +-83.5, the base's row about 14 mm under the flange, that is at Z 83 against our jack line at Z 88 (32.40 item 8). The LoRa jack at Y 0 would land on the nub; the LTE and WIFI P2P B jacks at Y +-96 and the SDR and VHF jacks at +-72 clear the nubs at +-83.5 by about 3 mm. **The LoRa jack moves to Y -24 on the east wall** (between the Iridium jack at -48 and the nub); `tools/case_wall_cutouts.py` and the render scene carry it, the wall template is regenerated, and the Iridium jack keeps its Maxtena helical (the 48 mm spacing rule of the old patch antenna no longer applies). The drill positions are checked against the case in hand before any hole is made (the used 1450 arrives after 7 Sep).

### 32.48 The owner's nine render and design items of 6 Sep 2026 17:30 (answers, rulings, the sixth render set)

1. **"A stupid tiny antenna on the right side of the case."** It is the Maxtena M1621HCT-P-SMA helical of the RockBLOCK 9704 (49 x dia 19 mm, 32.45) on the Iridium jack, drawn after the 16:20 instruction to depict the 9704 antenna properly; it is that small. From this set on the standard views carry no antennas at all (item 9), and a separate family shows all nine.
2. **"The four rods extend beyond the top cover."** No rationale: a scene error. The four M3 rods stand on the dock strip's nuts and end 5 mm above the B15 nuts (Z about 62); the scene drew them 118 mm tall, through the face. Fixed (rods 64 mm).
3. **SOS and ZEROIZE protected.** Both APEM 5636ADKB-2V locking toggles get a hinged safety cover on the plate, closed in every view (red on SOS, yellow on ZEROIZE); the plate holes do not change (the cover's base sits under the toggle nut). **Part pick owed:** the APEM 5000 catalogue on file only refers to "security guards, see Miscellaneous and Accessories section D", which is not filed, and NKK's accessories document on file (`vendor/switches/nkk-accessories-hardware.pdf`) lists dust covers and caps (AT4000 series), not guards; a hinged safety cover for a 6.35 mm (1/4-40) bushing toggle is to be picked from the makers' accessory sheets (APEM section D, NKK toggle guards) before the plate marking is final.
4. **The display shows the MeshSat touchscreen** (the owner's screenshot of 6 Sep 15:14 UTC from the tesseract kit, 1280 x 720, now `v2/cad/render/ui.png`). The sixth set still rendered the display black: the textured screen object sat 0.5 mm inside the display body, under its opaque glass, since the first 1450 set; the seventh set (18:10, 6bca935) has it on the glass and the dashboard shows in every face view.
