### 32.52 The MESHSAT-830 architecture (7 Sep 2026 00:35; Stage 1 of the approved plan)

**The owner's requirement (7 Sep 2026 00:30, verbatim in substance):** the three CM5 exist to avoid a single point of failure; if one module fails in software or hardware the other two continue; the board must be agnostic of which modules are present, how many (one, two or three) and in which slots; every device is visible to all three modules at once; the operating system on each module decides whether to adopt a device, the HAL (`cubeos/hal`, its `DeviceSupervisor` routes hot-plug events to the drivers) takes over, and k3s runs on top. The owner asked the session to design it ("I don't know how to design this"); the design below is the session's, recorded under that requirement, with the owner's veto.

**Plain words first.** Three computers in one box can all share one thing without help: the network. Everything else (USB, PCIe, the little radio buses) belongs to one computer at a time. So the kit is built like a small server rack: three identical slots, each with its own network port, its own drive, its own USB ports and one card slot; the radios and sensors are USB devices plugged into those ports; the software on whichever module has a device shares it to the others over the network, and if a module dies the devices on it are lost until it is back, while the other modules keep running with what they hold. The wiring makes every slot the same, so a module can go into any slot and the kit boots with one, two or three of them.

**1. The fabric.**
- **Ethernet:** a five-port Gigabit switch chip on B16 (Microchip KSZ9567 class, sheet owed to the laptop session): one port per slot, one to the sealed wall port with PoE out, one spare header. Every module, every service and every shared device travels here.
- **Storage:** one NVMe M.2 M-key 2242 per slot on the slot's PCIe lane through a one-to-two switch (ASMedia ASM1182e class), the second port of that switch a card slot; k3s replicates the storage across the drives (Longhorn or equivalent, a software issue), so maps, recordings and logs survive a module.
- **Cards:** slot 1 an M.2 E-key for the AW7915-AED WiFi link card, slot 2 an M.2 B-key 3052 for the 5G module, slot 3 an M.2 M-key 2280 spare (a third drive or an AI accelerator). The two cascaded four-port switches of 32.49 items 13 and 14 are replaced by these three one-to-two switches; the internal PCIe connector goes (a spare M.2 in slot 3 serves).
- **USB:** each slot's USB 3 pair into a four-port USB 3 hub (two internal device ports on headers, one to a shared internal expansion header, one for the slot's own devices); every radio and sensor is a USB device on one of those ports; the wall USB host port hangs on slot 1's hub. The HAL shares USB and serial devices to the other modules over the network (USB-over-IP and serial-over-IP: a HAL issue), so every module sees every device, adoption is a software choice, and the physical owner is a cabling choice written in the HAL configuration, not a board rule.
- **Display:** the three HDMI outputs into a three-input HDMI switch (TMDS switch parts, sheet owed) feeding the Xenarc; the panel controller selects the input of the module that runs the kiosk; touch over USB through the hub of that module.
- **Time:** the LG290P's pulse and the DCF77 pulse fanned out by buffers to a GPIO of every slot; chrony on each module; the holdover RTC on the panel controller's bus.
- **Panel and sensors:** two RP2040-class controllers as USB devices: the **panel controller** (the two expanders' job: LEDs, switches, sounder, the e-paper, the ambient light sensor, blackout and NVG lighting, the HDMI input select, the heartbeats, and the hardware EMCON and ZEROIZE logic that does not depend on any module: EMCON gates every transmitter rail and the PA bias, ZEROIZE wipes the secure element and asserts the disk-key wipe line) and the **sensor controller** (inside and outside climate, water, gas, motion, lightning, Geiger, the air mixer fan). Both are hot-pluggable USB devices the HAL adopts like any other.
- **Radios as USB devices:** LG290P and both E72 through USB-serial bridges (CP2102N class) on B16; RockBLOCK 9704 on its USB-C; LimeSDR Mini on USB 3; the QMX HF module on its USB-C; the camera a USB camera behind a plate window; the APRS board D8 a USB set (an SA868 control bridge and a USB audio codec in place of the I2S WM8960, so Direwolf runs on any module); the 1 W LoRa module on a slot's SPI header with its control lines, adopted by that module's meshtasticd (a second module in another slot is the cheap way to make LoRa survive a module loss; recorded as an option).
- **Secure element:** on the panel controller's I2C, reachable by every module through the HAL; ZEROIZE wipes it once for all.

**2. Distribution of the devices over the slots (the cabling written in the HAL configuration; any of it may move):** slot 1: WiFi link card, NVMe, LG290P bridge, the wall USB port, the camera; slot 2: 5G module, NVMe, RockBLOCK, the Zigbee E72, the panel controller; slot 3: spare M.2, LimeSDR, the HF module, the Thread E72, the sensor controller, D8's USB set, the LoRa module on its SPI. A lost slot 1 loses WiFi link, GNSS and camera; a lost slot 2 loses 5G, Iridium and Zigbee; a lost slot 3 loses SDR, HF, Thread, APRS and LoRa; the network, the panel logic in hardware, the display switch and the storage replica survive any single loss.

**3. Power budget (typical / peak, from the 32.49 table extended):** three CM5 18 / 36 W, Xenarc 6 / 10, WiFi card 3 / 10, 5G 3 / 10, LimeSDR 3 / 3, LoRa 0.5 / 6.5, RockBLOCK 0.5 / 5, HF module 1 / 12, APRS with the PA 1.5 / 75, switches, hubs, bridges and controllers 6 / 8, sensors and panel 2.5 / 2.5, PoE and USB-C outlets 0 / 90 when used, conversion losses 12 percent: **about 50 W typical, about 200 W peak without the outlets, up to 290 W with them.** One BB-2590 gives 5 to 6 hours typical, 8 to 9 dimmed. Rails on A22: the 14.4 V node (pack or charger); 13.8 V at 8 A (PA, monitor, PoE); 5 V at 15 A (three CM5 at up to 5 A each, hubs, USB devices, LoRa, sensors); 3.3 V at 6 A (cards, switches, bridges); 12.0 V at 1.5 A regulated for the HF module (the QMX must not see 13.8 V); the EMCON gates on the 3.3 V and 5 V branches of the WiFi card, the 5G module, the LoRa module, the RockBLOCK, the HF module and on the PA's VGG.

**4. Floor plans.** A22 240 x 160 mm (the rods stay at (+-110.5, +-73); the west 45 mm of A21's outline goes to the 2590 cradle; the south band keeps nine SMP-MAX at Y -66; the wide-range input and filter at the back-wall corner near the connector plate, the charger, the four converters in the `rail()` pattern, PoE and PD near the plate, the D8 mezzanine site 100 x 80 east of centre). B16 330 x 200 mm on six layers: the three CM5 sites in a row along the north band with their coolers (each site 60 x 45, receptacles on the 33 x 48 hole pattern), under each site its one-to-two switch, M.2 M-key 2242 and card slot; the USB 3 hubs and bridges along the middle; the Ethernet switch chip and its magnetics near the east edge toward the plate; the LimeSDR bay and the HF bay in the south-east; the RockBLOCK site, LG290P, both E72 and the LoRa module along the south band with their pigtails to the dock nests; the two controllers near the panel ribbon; the HDMI switch near the plate pass-through. C7 as in 32.51 (no aperture, the Xenarc cutout and VESA holes, headset holes, light window, camera window, the PDi flex, the panel ribbon to the panel controller). D8 100 x 80 on the mezzanine: SA868, the RA30H1317M1 on its flange to the heat column, T/R relay, low-pass filter, the USB audio codec and control bridge, two headset paths. E6 278 x 60: nine float clamps (the same X list as A22's sites), the 14.4 V bus from the cradle's cable to the block, the wide-range input entry, solar entry, the floor water strips, the tamper switch input.

**5. Walls.** End walls at Z 88: west VHF -72, WIFI 2.4 -24, GNSS +24, SDR +72; east LTE-5G main -96, IRIDIUM -48, LORA -24, WIFI P2P A +48, WIFI P2P B +96; the second 5G jack (diversity) at west Y -100 (the LTE label becomes 5G MAIN); the HF jack (BNC) at east Y +20 between LORA and WIFI P2P A once the nub check allows, else on the back plate; two 5G jacks are the working number until the RM520N-GL hardware design arrives (four would need the back plate). The vent for the outside sensors in the west wall at Y +100, Z 60. The back plate grows to 80 x 82 for the 38999 pair, the sealed Ethernet, the sealed USB-C and the ground stud.

**6. Heat.** The PA's flange bolts to an aluminium column rising from D8 through the backer's void to the underside of the face plate (`v2/cad/pa_heat_column.py`), about 20 x 20 mm section, 45 W at key-down at APRS duty; the three CM5 coolers exhaust into the case; the sensor controller runs an internal air mixer fan on the inside climate reading; the plate is the kit's heatsink and the test plan measures it.

**Decisions taken by the session under the owner's requirement (veto open):** the HF module is the assembled QMX unit in a bay (32.51); two 5G jacks until the hardware design says otherwise; the camera is a USB camera board behind a plate window on slot 1's hub; the PA heat goes to the plate; the lid tablet bracket sits over the west third of the lid (switch and e-paper zone), clear of the Xenarc box; the LoRa module stays SPI on slot 3 with a second module as the redundancy option.

### 32.53 Rulings of 7 Sep 2026 00:55 (owner): no vent opening anywhere, IP68 fans inside, the monitor's speaker, the outside sensors in a sealed pod

**The questions (owner, 00:40 to 00:50):** "a beeper/speaker?", "IP67/68/69 fans on the top board?", then "TLDR can one or two or three CM5 work fine inside the case without any holes to vent the hot air?" **The ruling (00:52): "ok good then no holes anywhere -> continue the work".**

**Thermal basis given with the answer (estimates, deployed with the lid open, monitor on, radios idle; the test plan's E3 measures them):** the plate (0.091 m2, anodised) sheds about 1 W/K by convection and radiation at a 30 to 40 K rise; the walls (about 0.22 m2 of side wall plus 0.135 m2 of floor, polypropylene 3 to 4 mm whose conduction is not the limit) add about 1.1 W/K with still air inside and about 2.0 W/K when internal fans couple the inside air to them; total about 2.1 W/K still, about 3.0 to 3.3 W/K with fans. Rise of the inside air over ambient: one CM5 (about 30 W) +14 K still, +10 K with fans; two (about 38 W) +18 / +12; three loaded (about 50 W) +24 / +16. The CM5 die runs 20 to 50 K over the inside air depending on its cooler's airflow, so at 40 C ambient three loaded modules sit at the 85 C throttle point with their fans and throttle without; at 25 C every case is comfortable. The 200 W peak (PA key-down) lasts minutes and goes into about 8 to 10 kJ/K of thermal mass, about +10 K transient. A black plate in full sun absorbs about 60 W, more than the electronics: the kit runs shaded. Lid closed, only the walls and the lid work (about 1.5 to 2 W/K with fans): one module is fine, three loaded modules at 40 C are not; the closed-lid transport mode is the reduced mode (monitor off, cluster idle). A vent would buy a few kelvin and cost the IP67 construction.

**What the ruling settles:**

1. **No vent opening anywhere** in the case skin, the plate or the connector plate: no through-plate fan, no membrane vent plug. Peli's own pressure equalisation valve stays (it is the case's, a membrane, and the altitude test E9 relies on it). The sealed pass-throughs (antenna jacks, the 38999 pair, Ethernet, USB-C, the headset jacks, the sensor pod receptacle) are connectors, not vents.
2. **Internal fans, IP68 rated:** one fan per CM5 cooler on its slot's fan header, two mixer fans under the plate on the sensor controller, speed from the inside climate reading; IP68 because the inside air cycles through the humidity test and condenses on cold walls, not for dust. Part pick owed (Sunon or Delta IP68 series, 40 and 60 mm; runner research pass three).
3. **The Xenarc 709GNK's built-in waterproof speaker is the kit's loudspeaker** (volume and mute in its menu, audio over HDMI; manual on file): the UI, spoken alerts and net monitoring; the two headset jacks stay the private audio and PTT path; blackout mutes the speaker and the sounder. No separate speaker.
4. **Sensor 8 of 32.50 loses its vent:** the outside climate and UV sensors (BME280, AS7331) go into a sealed pod bolted to the outside of the back-wall connector plate, on an M8 sealed receptacle (IP67 mated), with a UV-transparent window and a shade cap; the pod is a printed part with a gasket (`v2/cad/sensor_pod.py`, Stage 5). The inside pressure against the pod's outside pressure remains the seal check.
5. `V2-SPEC.md` takes the speaker in its audio row, the fans and the no-vent rule in its thermal section, the pod in its sensor paragraph, and five IP68 fans (+50) and the pod (+10) in the cost estimate.

### 32.55 The A22 power tree of the 14.4 V node (7 Sep 2026 01:10; from the TI sheets on file, for the Stage 2 generator)

**Node.** The BB-2590/U's two 14.4 V sections in parallel (10.0 to 16.8 V; 10 A continuous and 18 A peak by the pack's rating) are the kit's node `VBAT`: fused at the cradle cable (30 A MAXI blade), reverse-protected by an LM74700 ideal-diode controller with its FET, switched by the main power control (LTC2954 on a P-FET pair, as A21). Every load runs from `VBAT`; there is no NVDC path and no BATFET in the load path: the charger charges the node and, while shore is present, carries the load up to its own limit. The three TPS61288L boosts of the 1S node go.

**Inputs.** (1) Shore and vehicle, 9 to 36 V, through the wide-range front end on A22: LM74700 reverse polarity, LM5069 hot-swap with under and over-voltage limits (9 V, 40 V) and a current limit, the MIL-STD-461 class line filter (common-mode choke, X and Y capacitors, an SMCJ transient clamp), then an LM5176 four-switch buck-boost regulating a 20 V `VIN_BUS` at up to 5 A (100 W). (2) Solar into the same 20 V bus through the E6 tracker. (3) The charger BQ25731 from `VIN_BUS` (its input range is 3.5 to 24 V) to the 4S node at up to 8 A; the pack's own SMBus gauge (both sections) is read by the host through a PCA9548 segment and sets the charge window; the pack's thermistor line goes to the charger's TS pin. The shore inhibit of PANEL.md section 9 becomes the charger's enable.

**Rails from `VBAT`.**

| Rail | Part | Load | Enable and monitor |
|---|---|---|---|
| `+5V_S1`, `+5V_S2`, `+5V_S3` | one TPS56637 (6 A) per CM5 slot, 5.1 V | the module and its cooler fan | enable from the panel controller (an empty slot stays off; a slot can be off while the others run); INA226 per rail |
| `+5V_DEV` | TPS56637, 6 A | the USB devices behind the three hubs (bridges, controllers, LoRa module, camera), the LimeSDR bay and the RockBLOCK through their own TPS2596 switches | INA226 |
| `+3V3`, `+3V3_RF` | TPS62933 (3 A) each | logic; the LG290P, two E72, the 5G module's supply switch | `+3V3_RF` and the module switches gated by EMCON |
| `+13V8_PA` | LM5176 buck-boost, 13.8 V at 6 A | the RA30H1317M1 on D8 | enable = EMCON gate AND the software hold; INA226 |
| `+12V_HF` | TPS55288 buck-boost, 12.0 V at 2 A | the QMX (never 13.8 V) | enable = EMCON gate |
| `VMON`, `VHEAT` | `VBAT` through a TPS2596 eFuse each | the Xenarc (10 to 35 V input, under 10 W); the pack heater | HEAT_EN as PANEL.md section 11; VMON follows blackout |
| `+54V_POE` | LM5176 in boost, 54 V at 0.6 A | the TPS23861 PSE for the wall Ethernet port | software |
| USB-C PD outlet | TPS55288 (5 to 20 V at up to 3.25 A, set over I2C by the TPS25750) | the outlet | the PD controller; limited to 45 W while the PA keys |

**EMCON gates (hardware, from the panel controller's EMCON line, each ANDed with the HAL's hold):** `+13V8_PA` enable and the PA's VGG on D8; `+12V_HF` enable; the 5G module's supply switch and W_DISABLE; the WiFi card's 3.3 V buck enable on B16 and its W_DISABLE; the LoRa module's supply switch; the RockBLOCK's 5 V switch; the two E72's `+3V3_RF`; the LimeSDR bay switch.

**Budget.** 50 W typical, 200 W peak, 290 W with the outlets (32.52 item 3): 4 to 17 A from the node at 12 V, inside the pack's 18 A peak; the dock block's four CELL+ and four return pins (Mill-Max 9 A class) carry 36 A, adequate; the outlets drop to their minimum contract while the PA keys. Fuses: pack 30 A, vehicle input 10 A, PA rail 10 A blade; the PoE and PD paths are electronic. Shunts: 5 mOhm on the slot rails, 2 mOhm on the PA rail.

**I2C on A22.** INA226 at 0x40 (S1), 0x41 (S2), 0x44 (S3), 0x45 (DEV), 0x46 (PA), 0x47 (PoE) (the old SDR, LTE and WiFi monitors of those addresses go with B15); the BQ25731 at 0x6B (the BQ25792's address; only one is fitted); a PCA9548 mux isolates the pack's two SMBus sections, the TPS25750 and the TPS23861 on their own segments; the two A22 expanders stay at 0x21 and 0x24.

### 32.56 A22 floor plan, the PA on the plate, eleven blind-mate paths (7 Sep 2026 01:17; Stage 2 numbers for `gen_pcb_a.py`, `gen_pcb_a3.py`, `check_pcb_a.py`, `case_wall_cutouts.py`, `panel1450.py`)

**Outline.** 240 x 160 mm, X -120 to +120, Y -80 to +80 (case frame), corner radius 5, four layers; the rods stay at (+-110.5, +-73) with their 9 mm nut keep-outs. The west 45 mm of A21 (X -165 to -120) is the BB-2590/U cradle's floor (32.49 item 12).

**The PA module leaves D8 for the face plate.** B16 (330 x 200) covers the whole frame window over A22, so no column can rise from a mezzanine under it to the plate. The RA30H1317M1's copper flange bolts flat to the underside of the aluminium face plate (two PEM S-M3 nuts pressed into the plate, thermal compound), inside the backer's void, over a low-profile zone of B16 (the M.2 card area, cards 2 to 4 mm tall; the plate's underside is at Z 98.4, the module body 9.9 mm, B16's top at about Z 56); the plate is the heatsink (3 mm, 0.7 kg, 660 J/K: a 20 s key-down at 45 W warms the local patch about 15 K; the average at APRS duty is a few watts). Its leads run around B16's edge (10 mm of gap between B16 and the frame window on each side): the 13.8 V pair from A22's `J_PA` (JST-VH, 16 AWG), VGG from D8's bias gate, and two RG-316 coax (drive from D8's exciter, output back to D8's low-pass filter and transmit-receive relay, then the blind-mate pigtail). D8 keeps the SA868 exciter, the LPF, the relay, the codec set and the PTT and EMCON logic; `pa_heat_column.py` of the plan is replaced by `pa_plate_mount.py` (the two plate holes and the lead routing in `panel1450.py`). Lid budget: the module sits under the plate, so nothing changes on top.

### 32.57 A22 generator decisions (7 Sep 2026 02:10; the first A22 pre-route runs on the rented box 50107044)

Written while the A22 chain (`full_a22.sh`: `gen_sch_a.py`, `build_sch.sh`, `gen_pcb_a.py`, `check_pcb_a.py`, `gen_pcb_a3.py`, escapes, joins, fanout, pre-route DRC) was brought to its gate on the box. The schematic is 417 parts and 250 nets with no single-pin net; the placed board 397 footprints; the numeric gate passes; the routeflow profile is `routeflow/a22.json` (1.9.0, single thread, In1 as the ground plane layer with GND as a plane net, finish `finish_a22.sh` into `meshsat-pcb-a-revA-A22`).

**Part swaps against 32.55, all for buildability (standard packages that KiCad's library carries and JLCPCB stocks):**

| Function | 32.55 pick | A22 generator | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Slot and device 5 V rails | TPS56637 (VQFN-HR-10 RPA0010A) | Diodes AP64500SP-13 (5 A, 3.8 to 40 V, SO-8 with pad; C2070920, 3,946 in stock, 1.74 USD; `diodes/diodes-ap64500.pdf`) | the hot-rod land pattern is not in KiCad's library and would have to be drawn by hand from the sheet; the AP64500 is a plain SO-8 EP with a 40 V input, 5 A, and a PG-less enable |
| HF 12 V rail | TPS55288 (VQFN-HR-26 RPM0026A, I2C) | a fourth LM5176 stage (FB 140k/10k) | same land-pattern reason; the LM5176 stage is already the pattern of the board (front end, PA, PoE) |
| USB-C PD outlet | TPS25750D (WQFN-38 DRJ, split thermal pads) with a TPS55288 on I2C, 65 W | TI TPS25740A (VQFN-24 RGE, C544309, 2,954 in stock, 1.53 USD; `ti/ti-tps25740.pdf`) with a fifth LM5176 stage: 5 V idle, 9 V and 15 V on request (45 W at 3 A); CTL2 and CTL1 (open drain) switch R(FBL2) 21.0k and R(FBL1) 14.0k in parallel with the stage's 20k bottom resistor (sheet section 9.1.4); GDNG drives the VBUS N-FET, DSCG discharges through 43 Ohm, GD tied to VPWR through 1M with 700k to ground (9.1.3), VDD from the device rail | the TPS25740B (65 W, 20 V) has no stock; the TPS25750's package needs a hand-drawn footprint; 45 W charges phones and tablets and most laptops at 15 V; the outlet returns to 65 W when the B variant is buyable |
| I2C mux | PCA9548 | none | its only clients (the PD controller's I2C target, the TPS55288) are gone |
| PA rail eFuse | TPS25982 | none | the LM5176's own current limit and the EMCON gate on its enable pin do the job; the eFuse would have added a hot-rod-free but large part for no function |

**Other decisions taken in the generator:** the sensor board S1 folds into E6 (the floor strip carries the RP2040 sensor controller, the water strips, the pack cable entry with its 30 A blade, the shore protection and filter, the solar tracker; its USB reaches B16 through two dock contacts and the A to B ribbon); `J_DOCK` map: 1 to 4 VIN_RAW (9 to 36 V from E6), 5 to 7 GND, 8 SHORE_INHIBIT (A22 to E6's hot-swap enable), 9 and 10 USB of E6's controller, 11 GND, 12 spare (read on the 0x21 expander); `J_AB1` is 2x13: 1 PI_SHDN_REQ, 2 PI_KILL, 3 GND, 4 and 5 USB D8, 6 GND, 7 and 8 USB E6, 9 GND, 10 and 11 USB wall (the wall USB-C's data pair on its way to B16), 12 GND, 13 SDA, 14 SCL, 15 EXP_INT, 16 TR_APRS, 17 EMCON_HW, 18 TX_INHIBIT_n, 19 to 21 SLOT_EN1..3, 22 ZEROIZE_HW, 23 GND, 24 SHORE_INHIBIT, 25 spare, 26 GND; it sits at (-84, 73.5) rotated along X, 5.7 mm east of the rod nut; the pack heater and the monitor run from VBAT through TPS259631 eFuses; D8's 5 V through a third; the charger is inhibited by pulling ILIM_HIZ low (CHG_INHIBIT on the 0x21 expander) instead of the old SHORE_INHIBIT contact; the 0x24 expander reads the four LM5176 PGOOD lines and drives PD_EN; the INA226 addresses are 0x40, 0x41, 0x44, 0x45 (rails), 0x46 (PA), 0x47 (PoE); the MAIN button lead moved to the east strip at (110, -38) because the west edge is full; the fuse F1 sits at (-97, -52) and the test points beside it.

**Placement numbers that moved during the eight pre-route runs (recorded so the next generation starts from them):** the front end zone is Y 34 to 66 (the rod nut at (-110.5, 73) forbids Y 72), the charger zone Y -6 to 34, the PoE zone Y -44 to -6, the rails' ICs at Y 66 with their inductors at Y 54 and their input capacitors in a row at Y 58 to 63 between the ICs, the four rail monitors and the PA monitor in one row at Y 28 with the shunts below them, the 3.3 V buck at (-6, 31) with its inductor at (-6, 24), the PA stage in Y -14 to 20, the HF stage in X -46 to -16 and Y -48 to -22 with its small parts in the strip X -16 to -2, the control zone (LTC2954, the AND gates, the two expanders) in X -66 to -46 and Y -48 to -14, the PD stage and the eFuses in the north-east band with the controller at (10, 65), the mezzanine harness header along Y at (-8, 8) (its shroud is 29 mm long).

### 32.59 B16 generators, and what the first routes of A22 and E6 taught (7 Sep 2026 05:45; Stage 2 record for `gen_sch_b.py`, `gen_pcb_b.py`, `gen_pcb_b3.py`, `check_pcb_b.py`, `gen_footprints_b16.py`, `full_b16.sh`, `finish_b16.sh`, `routeflow/b16.json`; corrections to the A22 and E6 generators)

**B16 as generated (797 parts, 682 nets, three slot columns S1 X -98 to -38, S2 -36 to 32, S3 34 to 94, north band Y 32 to 88 for the modules).** Per slot: the Compute Module 5 on its receptacle pair, the PI7C9X2G404SL switch and the TUSB8041I hub side by side south of the cards (the switch's twelve 100 nF on the underside inside its pad ring), the NVMe M-key 2242 and the card socket at Y 25 with the cards extending south (S2's NVMe lies along X at the column's south end because the 3052 5G card takes the height; its SIM holders sit east of the card), two AP64500 3.3 V bucks (A the card socket on PCIE_PWR_EN, B switch, hub and NVMe following the module's 3.3 V), TPS62933 bucks for the 1.0 V switch core and the 1.1 V hub core, the flashing USB-C and the 5 V lead at the south edge, the fan header west of the module, the console and nRPIBOOT headers; the EEPROM, PMIC and power-button jumpers of B15 are gone and the SPI breakout exists on S3 only (the E22 hangs on it). Shared: the KSZ9897R block north-west (the RJ45 at the north edge, the H5007NL magnetics, the TPS23861 PoE injector with its FET; the switch strapped for I2C management by LED4_1 low), the QMX bay 63 x 95 along Y between the rods at X -162 to -99, Y -66 to 29, the LimeSDR bay X 130 to 161, Y -24 to 45 with its USB 3 receptacle at the south end, the RockBLOCK 9704 bracket at (139, -71) whose plate rides on 8 mm standoffs over rod nut R2, the two TS3DV642 display switches at the north-east corner and the HDMI receptacle at the south-east corner opening south, the E22 and the two E72 north-east (antennas to the north edge), the LG290P, the CR2032, the secure element, the holdover clock and the temperature sensor in the gap between the S2 and S3 coolers, the expanders and the EMCON gates in the gap between S1 and S2, the CP2102N bridges and the eFuses east of the columns, J_AB1 under the board at (113, -46). Test points on the north edge over the coolers.

**Decisions taken by the generator (owner rulings untouched):** (1) B16 is assembled on both sides: the decoupling and pull-ups of every slot sit on the underside beneath their ICs, never under a fine-pitch part (its escapes need the vias) and never under a through-hole header; the packer takes a `back` flag per region. (2) The QMX unit sits between the rods along Y; its 12 V lead runs from A22's J_HF straight to the unit's DC jack (no B16 part). (3) The 5G module's second SIM uses the B-key pins 40, 42, 44, 46 as the RM5xx series does; to confirm from the RM520N-GL hardware design (laptop research row) before an order, a wrong map only leaves SIM 2 dead. (4) The CP2102N bridges take their bus sense and regulator input from the rail of the slot whose hub carries them. (5) The hub ports: S1 the LimeSDR (USB 3), the panel controller, the camera, the RockBLOCK bridge; S2 the GNSS bridge, the two E72 bridges, the QMX lead; S3 D8, E6's controller, the wall USB-C, a spare header. (6) Hardware EMCON on B16: the WiFi and 5G cards through W_DISABLE1#, the LoRa module and the two E72 through rail switches, the LimeSDR and the RockBLOCK through their eFuse enables, all ANDed with EMCON_HW in 74LVC08 gates. (7) Kit I2C: the panel controller masters the bus over J_PANEL; B16 carries the pull-ups, the two PCA9555 (0x20, 0x25), the ATECC608B (0x60), the DS3231MZ (0x68), the TMP117 (0x49), the KSZ9897R and the TPS23861; nothing on B16 uses a module's I2C.

**Footprints written by `gen_footprints_b16.py`:** the M.2 M-key 2242 and B-key 3052 sockets (the B14 E-key land pattern with the notch of each key and the standoff at the card length minus 1.75), the Quectel LG290P (24 edge pads 1.5 x 0.8 on the 7 + 5 rows at 1.1 mm and the 5 x 11 ground matrix at 1.4 mm, hardware design figure 18), the Ebyte E22-900M30S (22 stamp-hole pads at 2.54 mm from the manual's section 3.3, host pads 3.2 x 1.4), the Pulse H5007NL (24 pins at 1.27 mm, land 0.76 x 1.9 on 12.70 / 16.51), and the two 128-pin QFPs with an exposed pad (10 x 10 for the KSZ9897R from Microchip's drawing, 6 x 6 drawn conservatively for the Diodes switch). Every one loads in pcbnew at the end of the generator. The placer centres a footprint's whole drawn box: an M.2 socket with its card outline lands with its body 13.65 (2230), 19.65 (2242) or 24.65 mm (3052) north of the target, which is why the fixed positions carry those offsets and the gate checks the standoff holes.

**A22, corrected before its route (7 Sep 2026 05:30):** (a) the power FETs were mapped with the three-pin `Q_NMOS_GDS` symbol onto the PowerPAK SO-8 land, whose pads 1 to 3 are the source, 4 the gate and 5 the drain tab: the gate and drain nets sat on source pins and the gate and drain pads carried nothing, on all 21 FETs of the LM5176 stages, the charger and the outlet switch. `nfet()` is a five-pin connector symbol now and `check_pcb_a.py` gates every PowerPAK's pad map. (b) On the box's KiCad 9.0.9 the router's DSN carried every root-sheet net (the `/NAME` form) in `kicad_default`: `GetEffectiveNetClass("/VBAT")` answers Default under both pattern forms of 32.39, while an explicit `netclass_assignments` entry is honoured; the placement generators of A22, B16 and E6 now write an explicit assignment for every net from the first matching pattern, so the class widths reach the router and the DRC. (c) With the classes enforced, class clearances above the 0.2 mm pad gap of a 0.65 mm pitch part fail inside the LM5176 and the TPS23861: the class clearances sit at the board minimum (0.127, NODE 0.15) and the 54 V nets at 0.18. (d) The edge band of E6 (below) is on A22 too; the CHS and POS packing regions start 3 mm off the west edge for a routing channel. (e) routeflow's `via_costs 100` remedy is withdrawn for boards with a plane net: on A22 round 3 it left the AP64500 exposed pads open and knotted the PoE stage (12 hard); `budget_rounds` is 1 and the session audits the leftovers.

**E6, corrected after its first two routes (11 and 15 opens, 3 edge violations):** an edge band on every copper layer (no tracks or vias within 0.5 mm of the outline, the routeflow remedy's advice), the float-clamp no-copper circles on the top face only (the clamp sits on the top; B.Cu routes under it), a CELL_F pour band on B.Cu along the west end and under the blade lands (the pack node reaches the fans and the monitor divider without router tracks), the monitor divider R42/R43 packed at the pack instead of the sensor cluster, the pack and fan regions 2 mm off the west edge, the controller region 2 mm taller. The stub router is not the tool for a board with more than a handful of opens: on E6 round 2 it closed six nets with 146 hard violations and was reverted.

**Owed:** the route results of A22, E6 and B16 (this section is written while they run), the B16 pair report, the bottom-side assembly line in the order notes and the cost rows of `V2-SPEC.md`, the B15 note that its J_FLASH opened into the board (rot 180 on a receptacle whose opening is at local +y; B16 uses rot 0), the appendix numbers of 32.58 that changed here (the column widths, the QMX bay, the RockBLOCK site, the HDMI corner).

### 32.60 The route campaign of the night, the D8 release, the C7 design (7 Sep 2026 08:15 CEST; Stage 2 and 3 record, MESHSAT-830)

Everything below ran on the rented CPU box 50107044 (two EPYC 9654), the boards in parallel under `tools/routeflow.py`, one Freerouting 1.9.0 attempt per round, single thread. The times are the box clock (UTC, two hours behind the record's headers).

**1. B16.** Run 1 died at the DSN export: the S2 placement lists of `gen_pcb_b3.py` carried six capacitor references twice (C225 to C227, C230 to C232, the small bucks' capacitors in both S2_RAIL and S2_SUP2), two footprints per reference, and KiCad's Specctra exporter refuses such a board without a message (`ExportSpecctraDSN` returns False, the route sees "no session"). Every placement generator now stops on a reference listed twice (the D8 generator caught its own R5 the same way an hour later). Run 2 has been routing since 04:26 UTC under a 240 minute limit; its result goes in 32.61.

**2. E6 (rounds 4 to 11).** The changes, in the order they were found: (a) In2 is a power layer in the DSN and the CELL_F, VIN_RAW, PV_P and TRK_OUT pours on it are DSN planes the router reaches by vias; the In2 GND pour went, because two zones whose outlines overlap would both be planes in the DSN (the exporter writes outlines, not fills). (b) The RP2040 (QFN-56, 0.4 mm) had 8 pads without escapes under the QFN scheme and every open of round 3 sat on one of them; the board takes the CM5IO scheme of the B boards (minimum via 0.40/0.20, hole clearance 0.19, every class at 0.127). (c) The packer keeps 2.2 mm around parts with sixteen or more fine pads (the escape rows splay that far), 1.4 around SOT and USON parts; U5 (the tracker) moved 1.2 mm west of its resistor row. (d) `prefanout.py` compared pad net names with the list as written, so a root-sheet label ("/CELL_F") never matched and only GND, a power symbol, ever got a via; that was why every round left the pack cluster's CELL_F pads open. It now strips the slash, tries diagonal candidates and offsets to 2.9 mm, uses the board's small via (0.45/0.25) instead of 0.8/0.4, keeps 0.5 mm from other-net pads instead of 0.75, puts the via in the pad when nothing else fits and a neighbouring pad allows it (the count is reported for the order notes), and gives the exposed pad of a fine-pitch part its via (the amplifier's pad on D8 sat on an island). (e) Fanout only for nets that have a plane or pour to land on: a pre-placed via of a net without one is one more target the router must reach (D8 went from 2 opens to 10 the round the rails were added). (f) The finish scripts no longer revert every stub-router closure when one of them adds a violation: `tools/stub_accept.py` removes the closures the DRC names (by item uuid, the whole chain of the closure) and keeps the rest; A22 had lost 8 good closures over one bad one, E6 6 over 2. Round 11 is routing with all of it.

**3. D8 released.** The APRS mezzanine generators (`gen_sch_d.py`, `gen_pcb_d.py`, `gen_pcb_d3.py`, `check_pcb_d.py`, `full_d8.sh`, `finish_d8.sh`, `routeflow/d8.json`) came back clean in run 7, round 2 (the `via_costs 100` remedy): 0 hard, 0 open, 119 router vias, 2576 tracks, 211 footprints, 133 nets; deliverable `v2/release/revA/boards/meshsat-pcb-d-revA-D8` (14 items, four copper layers in the gerber zip). Six ground vias sit in their pads (order note owed: JLC accepts via-in-pad on a prototype, the pads are 0603 grounds). The design as generated: J_HARN1 mirrors A22's J_MEZZ1 (1 GND, 2/3 the USB pair, 5 TR_APRS, 6 TX_INHIBIT_n, 7 PA_EN, 9/10 I2C, 11 EXP_INT, 12 +3V3, 14 ZEROIZE_HW, 15 AB_SPARE, the rest GND) and J_PWR1 takes +5V_D8; a TUSB2046B four-port hub (self-powered, no EEPROM, 6 MHz crystal with 27 pF and a 1.5k trim, 1.5k on DP0, 22 ohm series and 15k pull-downs per port) with the PCM2912A codec on port 1 (5 V bus, its own regulator feeding VDD and the VCC pins, 33 ohm series and 1.5k on D+, 6 MHz crystal, MAMP off, POWER low), a CP2102N on port 2 (the exciter's UART, RTS as the software PTT) and a spare header on port 3; the SA868 on its own castellated footprint (`NiceRF_SA868` in `meshsat.pretty`, 18 pads 1.6 x 2.6 at 4.45 mm: 1 AUDIO_ON low when receiving, 3 AF_OUT 700 mV, 5 PTT low, 6 PD, 7 H/L pulled low by PA_EN, 8 VBAT behind a ferrite, 12 ANT, 16/17 UART, 18 MIC_IN); the T/R relay Omron G6K-2F-Y (top view pins 8 7 6 5 over 1 2 3 4, coil 1 plus and 8 minus, poles 3-2-4 and 6-7-5 with 2 and 7 the rest contacts): at rest the exciter's ANT (3) meets the antenna SMA (6) through the rest contacts, keyed with the PA the exciter drives the 10 dB T-pad (27/36/27 ohm 2010) to the U.FL J_PAIN, and the PA output SMA J_PAOUT passes the 5-element low-pass (22p/68n/39p/68n/22p, 1206 500 V and 1812; values to be verified in MESHSAT-818) into the antenna; the PTT logic in 74LVC1G parts (KEY = any PTT AND TX_INHIBIT_n, PA_KEY = KEY AND PA_EN, the relay coil and the TPS22810 gate-bias switch on PA_KEY, TR_APRS from KEY through 100 ohm, the TX LED on KEY); a TPA6132A2 (G0 high, G1 low: 0 dB) drives both headset earpieces with the receive mix (AF_OUT and the codec's left output), a TLV9062 sums both headset microphones (33 dB, electret bias by solder jumper) with the codec's right output into MIC_IN; a PCA9555 at 0x26 on the harness 3.3 V reads COS, both PTT lines, KEY and PA_KEY and drives the exciter's PD, the amplifier's EN and the codec's mute through 2N7002 level stages; RF class 0.35 mm at 0.3 clearance, PWR 0.5, USB 0.2. The relay pin map and every pin table came from the sheets fetched to the scratchpad (Omron G6K, NiceRF SA868 V1, TI SLES230A, SLLS413L, SLOS553).

Two more findings of the morning (09:20 CEST).** (a) A ring of 0.4 mm escape vias around a QFN (the RP2040 on E6 and C7) fences the ground plane on every layer: the vias sit 0.8 mm apart, the fill needs 0.25 mm plus two clearances between them, so the copper under the part becomes an island on In1, In2 and both outer layers, and the exposed pad's ground reaches the outside only by luck. `join_adjacent_pins.py` now joins every ground pad of a part with an exposed pad to that pad by a locked track along the pad's own axis (a diagonal to the pad's centre grazed the neighbouring pins; the exposed pad's paste windows are not obstacles), so the island always has a way out through a pad's escape via. (b) The BB-2590/U does not fit at the west wall as ruled: the pack is 125.6 x 111 x 62 and can only lie with its 62 mm up (standing it is taller than the 98 mm under the plate); at the west wall its 62 mm has to run along X, and the floor there leaves 60 to 64 mm beside A22 (the 1450 floor is 360 wide, A22's west edge sits at X -120, the rods at X +-110.5). One of: the whole stack (rods, A22, B16, E6's rod holes) moves 5 mm east, or the pack goes into the external 2590 box on the back wall that 32.49 offered. A decision for the owner; the render scene leaves the west wall empty until then.

### 32.62 Ruling 7 Sep 2026 13:10 CEST (owner): the pack becomes a smaller one, MIL-STD if possible; the case stays the Peli 1450 at any cost (no change of case ever again)

The owner's words on the finding of 32.61 item 7: "a smaller pack == the BB-2590/U battery doesn't fit the 1450 == MIL-STD if possible == we do keep the 1450 at any cost; no change of peli-case ever again". So option (c) of 32.61 item 7 is closed for good, the BB-2590/U of 32.49 is withdrawn, and the pack is a smaller family that fits the pocket the board set leaves. **The pocket** (case frame, from `gen_pcb_a.py`, `gen_pcb_b.py`, `gen_pcb_e.py`, `panel1450.py` and the 1451-931 drawing): A22 spans X -120 to +120, B16 X -165 to +165 with its underside at Z 54.4 (top copper 56, 1.6 mm board) and a few millimetres of parts under it, the rods stand at (+-110.5, +-73), E6 spans X -149 to +118 and Y -113 to -45, the floor is 360 x 246 with the end walls drafting outward above it. That leaves, at the west wall, a box of about **58 x 160 x 48 mm** (X from -178 to -120, Y from -40 to +120, Z from 1 to 49) under B16's overhang and beside A22, plus the 31 mm wide strip west of E6's end over the full length at the same height. The pack lies along the west wall in that box, its cable to E6's `J_BATT` at the strip's west end, the heater mat under it if the family needs one; the SMBus charger (BQ25731) and the 14.4 V node of 32.55 stay as they are for a 4S pack, and the front end, the rails and the gates do not care. The research gate item: a rechargeable pack of the 14.4 V class (4S Li-ion, about 100 to 150 Wh) with an SMBus gauge, tested to MIL-STD-810 where a maker offers it, no more than 58 x 160 x 48 mm; the candidates and the pick follow in the next section, the cradle (`pack_cradle_2590.py` becomes `pack_cradle.py`) and the render after the pick.

**The research pass on the ruling (13:20 CEST).** The web search budget of the session was spent, so the makers' pages were read directly. RRC's standard smart packs (`rrc-ps.com`, SMBus, IEC 62133 and UL 2054, no MIL-STD statement): the RRC2054-2 is 14.4 V, 6.8 Ah, 98 Wh, 4S2P, 150.4 x 77.4 x 22.4 mm, 440 g; the RRC2024 14.4 V, 6.6 Ah, 95 Wh, 167.2 x 107.2 x 21.5 mm. Both are 77 mm or more in their second dimension, and the pocket is 58 mm wide and 48 mm high: no laptop-form smart pack fits, standing or lying. The military families (Bren-Tronics, Epsilor, Ultralife, Denchi) publish their radio and half-size packs behind product finders the fetch could not read; the half-size BB-2557/U (127 x 112 x 32) fails on the same 112 mm as the 2590, and the soldier-radio packs (BB-2588 class, 94 x 74 x 69) fail on height and hold about 70 Wh. **Finding:** no COTS pack of 100 Wh or more fits the pocket the board set leaves; the pack of this kit is built, not bought, and the MIL-STD part of the ruling is met by the kit's own qualification programme (`TEST-PLAN.md`) covering the pack.

**The second pocket.** The same reading of the floor plan gives a better pocket on the east side: E6 ends at X +118, so between A22's east edge (+120) and the east wall (+180) the floor is free over its whole length under B16's overhang: about **58 x 240 x 48 mm** (X +120 to +178, Y -120 to +120, Z 1 to 49), the six east-wall couplers at Z 88 well above it. The west pocket (58 x 160 x 48) stays for a second pack.

**The pack proposal (session decision under the ruling, veto open): a built 4S smart pack in the east pocket.** Cells 18650 in a 3 wide x 2 high x 3 long block (18 sites, 16 used as 4S4P: 3.5 Ah cells give 14.4 V, 14 Ah, about 200 Wh, about 850 g of cells) or 21700 in 2 x 2 x 3 (4S3P, 5 Ah cells: 15 Ah, 216 Wh); a BMS board of our own (project `pcb-p-pack`, phase P1) with a TI BQ40Z50-class SMBus 1.1 gas gauge and protection (the charger BQ25731 of A22 already speaks SMBus to it), the cell thermistor on the gauge, a 25 A blade at the terminal, the XT60 and the SMBus lead to E6's `J_BATT` and `J_SMB` (a 350 mm run along the front wall to the strip's west end; E6 stays as released), a printed enclosure with a fold-over lid on four M3 (`v2/cad/pack_4s.py`), the heater mat of 32.32 under it. The west pocket takes a second identical pack when wanted (about 150 Wh in 4S3P 18650), the two in parallel behind their own gauges. Energy: one east pack gives about 200 Wh against the 2590's 290; two packs about 350 Wh. This is the P1 generator of the next work block, after render set eight; the render shows the east pack as a stand-in box until then.

**P1, the pack BMS board, generated and routed (14:10 CEST).** `tools/gen_sch_p.py`, `gen_pcb_p.py`, `gen_pcb_p3.py`, `check_pcb_p.py`, `full_p1.sh`, `finish_p1.sh`, `routeflow/p1.json`; project `v2/ecad/pcb-p-pack`. The design: TI BQ4050 (SMBus 1.1 gauge with Impedance Track, primary protection and internal balancing for 1S to 4S; SLUSC67B filed as `vendor/battery/ti-bq4050.pdf`; JLCPCB C157570, 10933 in stock on 7 Sep) with the cell taps VC1 to VC4 through 100 ohm and 0.1 uF, BAT through 100 ohm, PACK and VCC through 1 kohm from the pack terminal, the coulomb counter across a 2 mohm 2512 shunt in the return (SRP on the cell side, SRN on the pack side, 100 ohm each), the block's 103AT thermistor on TS1 and the unused TS inputs held at 10k to VSS, PTC and PTCEN disabled, PRES pulled low (present), DISP low (no LEDs), no chemical fuse (the 25 A mini blade in a Keystone 3568 holder is the fuse); two CSD17570Q5B PowerPAK N-FETs in series on the high side with common drain (the charge FET's source at the fused cell terminal, the discharge FET's source at PACK+), 5.1 kohm gate drive and 10 Mohm gate-source; 0.1 uF ESD capacitors and an SMBJ20A across the terminals; the SMBus pair through 100 ohm and a USBLC6-2SC6 clamp; connectors J_CELL (JST-XH 1x5, the five tap wires, sense only), J_TS (JST-PH 1x2), J_SMB (JST-XH 1x4: SMBC, SMBD, GND, PRES) and four 2.5 mm2 solder lands for the block's B+ and B- straps and the pack's two 12 AWG leads. The board: 70 x 44 mm, two layers on the 2 oz stack, four M3 holes at (+-32, +-19) for the enclosure bosses; the power path never travels in router tracks (the A21 rule): B+ land, blade, charge FET, discharge FET, PACK+ land along the north edge and B- land, shunt, PACK- land along the south edge as locked 3 mm bands on both faces with 0.8/0.4 stitch vias (the FET source pins reach their band through three 0.6 mm stubs, the band stopping 4.6 mm before the pins so the gate pin keeps its clearance; every via at least 2.2 mm from a band end for the lands' 2.4 mm holes); a ground pour on the underside; classes PWR 1.0/0.3, GNDC 0.5/0.127, SENSE 0.4/0.127, Default 0.25/0.127. Placement lessons on the way (five pre-route rounds): the packer's row logic overflows a 6 mm wide test-point strip (two points per row), the SolderWire lands' courtyards want 6.7 mm from the M3 holes' courtyards, the fuse holder's 16.6 mm body wants its own 1.2 mm from the land, and the 2 oz stack's 0.5/0.3 vias push the escape stubs to the 0.127 class clearance. Route: 1.9.0 single thread, round 1 clean but two opens the stub router could not hold (its closures onto the wide bands did not register as connections), round 2 with via_costs 100 routed everything: **0 hard, 0 open, 60 footprints, 800 tracks, 119 vias**; deliverable `v2/release/revA/boards/meshsat-pcb-p-revA-P1` (commit 80eb218). The enclosure `v2/cad/pack_4s.py` (`release/revA/case/pack-4s/`): box 56 x 236 x 44 with a 2 mm lid on four M3 corner posts (46 over all), 2 mm walls, the 4S4P cell block pocket at one end, the board bay on four M3 bosses at the other, a 14 x 12 cable notch in the end wall, two 18 mm strap slots in the floor; about 94 g of PETG. Bench work that stays: the cell block welding (0.15 x 8 mm nickel), the gauge's golden image from TI's bqStudio over the SMBus before the lid goes on, the pack's own qualification in the kit's programme.

**A22 run 12 closed by hand (14:32 CEST).** Run 12 (120 passes; the 250-pass run 11 had converged by pass 150 and was stopped before its limit could eat the session) came back with 11 hard and 15 opens; the finish's knot removal and stub router left 0 hard and 3 opens: VBUS20 (the LM5176 U3's pad 3, whose escape chain had lost its via to the dangling clean-up and ended 1.6 mm from the surviving via of the pad-1 chain, with the CH_ACN escape in between), HEAT_EN and HEAT_FLT (the PCA9555 U27's pins 6 and 16 to the heater eFuse U22, 130 mm across the board, both escapes gone the same way). The closures: VBUS20 by `tools/hand_route.py` (locked tracks along waypoints with layer changes as vias, DRC-tested on a copy): a via at the chain's end and 1.6 mm of In2 under the CH_ACN stub to the pad-1 via. HEAT_FLT by the stub router with a board-wide window (`STUB_WIN_SCALE=25 STUB_GRID=0.2 STUB_MAXN=80000000`: 342 tracks, 3 vias, a 134 mm path). HEAT_EN could not leave its pad: the EXP2_SP7 spare's router track and via sat 0.13 mm in front of it with D8_EN and MON_EN under the body and PD_PGOOD on the underside; the seven EXP2_SP7 items in the lane were ripped, the pad got a hand hop (1.2 mm west on F.Cu, a via at x -53.9 clear of PD_PGOOD, 0.3 mm of In2), and the board-wide stub router then closed HEAT_EN (340 tracks, 2 vias, 132 mm) and re-closed EXP2_SP7 (51 tracks, 1 via). Board: 0 hard, 0 open before the finish; the finish (quality pass, pair gate, legends, the A gate) and the deliverable follow. Lesson for the pipeline: the stub router's default 8 and 15 mm windows are for stubs; with the window scaled to the board and a 0.2 mm grid it is a serviceable single-net router for the last opens (the cells stay under 4 million per layer on 240 x 160), and the dangling clean-up after an unknot must not delete the escape via of a pad whose net is still open (the escapes of U3, U27 and U22 were all removed as "unused" and had to be redrawn by hand).

**A22 released (14:38 CEST).** Deliverable `v2/release/revA/boards/meshsat-pcb-a-revA-A22` (commit cbe7598): 0 hard, 0 open, 397 footprints (376 on top, 21 on the underside: the spring-pin connector, the pre-charge pin, the eight pack contacts and the eleven blind-mate receptacles), 4248 tracks, 892 vias, six layers on JLC06161H-3313, the quality pass accepted (segments 4947 to 4238). E5 rebuilt from the final A22 the same minute (`meshsat-pcb-e5-revA-E5`, 33785fb; `build_e5.sh` reads A22's board for the targets). The GLBs of A22 and E5 are exported for the renders. Of the set, B16 alone still routes (run 3 with the optimizer capped, in its autoroute passes since 12:43 CEST).


## 32.63 Render set eight and the B16 route campaign (7 Sep 2026 evening)

**Render set eight is published (18:33 CEST, commit ec104ee, 50 views in `v2/images/concept-1450/` with the index in its README, the zip on the revA release).** The set shows the MESHSAT-830 kit in the Peli 1450: the face plate with the Xenarc monitor and the toggle covers, the three CM5 slots with their coolers and M.2 cards on B16, the eleven blind-mate receptacles on A22, the 4S pack block in the east pocket, the QMX tray on the lid's inner face (`lid-inside`), the five-step assembly sequence, the antenna family, the closed views. The board models come from the KiCad GLB export with parts and pads only (tracks are not exported), so the B16 model was taken from its pre-route board and renders identically to the routed one; the six GLBs are committed (6851b27) and replace the previous generation's. Rendered on an 8x H100 box in 28 minutes (scene build 5 minutes, 50 views at about 20 s each), box destroyed at 18:33 CEST.

**B16 routing facts (Freerouting 1.9.0, single thread, In1 and In4 as power layers, 1452 connections after the plane fanout on a 330 x 200 mm board with four routing layers).** The router writes no session until every autoroute pass has ended, so a time limit that cuts the passes leaves nothing: 100 passes exceeded 4 hours (run 3, 10:43 to 14:43 UTC), 40 passes exceeded 1 h 50 min, 10 passes exceeded 1 h 40 min. Thread dumps taken with SIGQUIT showed every process inside the autoroute passes (maze search and connectivity recursion), none idle and none in the optimiser. Three passes took 1 h 42 min and left 2 hard and 252 open (the one-pass diagnostic of the morning had left about half of the connections open, spread over the whole board, not a blocked region: 25 percent rail nets, 33 percent buses and pairs, 42 percent other signals). Ground is not the load: 54 of the 920 ground pads and 11 of the 122 slot-rail pads had no plane via after the fanout. The four +5V pours on In4 are now kept in the DSN as planes (`FR_PLANE_NETS`), which takes 122 pins off the wire list; the per-slot 3.3 V and core rails (about 500 pads) have no pour and are wired, and their pads are interleaved with the signal parts over each slot column, so an In4 island per rail would need a placement pass, not a zone edit (owed as the B17 power-copper pass beside A23). The route continues from the three-pass session in five-pass chunks (`cont_route.sh`, which now keeps the plane nets and the power layers and reads the optimiser threshold `FR_OIT`; driver `b16_chunks.sh` in the session scratchpad), each chunk a checkpoint, beside a 20-pass and a 5-pass copy and routeflow's 100-pass round 2 with an 8 hour limit; the first board with 0 hard and 0 open, or the best one for the stub router and the hand closures, becomes the release.

### 32.64 Audit of the fab-ready methodology against the Quilter interview (8 Sep 2026 01:09 CEST; MESHSAT-862; owner request of 00:35, "audit extensively the methodologies we are currently using to achieve 100 percent confidence graduation, aka fab ready")

**Method.** Three read-only surveys of the repository (the routing quality programme, the gates and the simulation plan, the placement method and the audit history), a critic pass, a web check of the outside tools, and a re-verification by grep of every script defect named below before it was written. The rubric is the interview of Sergiy Nesterenko (Quilter) with Zach Peterson (OnTrack, 27 May 2026): layout is a geometry, physics and manufacturing problem and never a language problem; whether a layout is good is a computable question, judged against physics and DRC and never against what a human would draw; constraints first (currents, bypass capacitor to pin, pairs with impedance targets, rooms, keep-outs, a clearance matrix), and the user's first job is to confirm the tool understood them; iterate like a senior engineer over a junior, hourly; the honest bar is a board good enough to test the schematic, not a production layout (Quilter's own flagship, an i.MX 8M Mini SOM and baseboard of 843 parts and 5141 pins on eight layers, reached 98.4 to 98.7 percent completion with 12 and 26.5 hours of human clean-up); specialised solvers beat general models and the right basis function matters more than compute.

**Outside tools (web, 8 Sep 2026).** Quilter takes and returns KiCad projects, is priced per unrouted pin per project, does placement and routing with rooms and fixed parts, and shipped BGA fan-out in 2026. DeepPCB (InstaDeep) routes only, through a cloud service and an open-source KiCad plugin since May 2026 whose public tier stops at 1,200 airwires (B16 has 1,452 connections). Antmicro's `kicad-si-simulation-wrapper` and `gerber2ems` run openEMS on KiCad 9 boards including differential pairs. PCBWorld (arXiv 2607.05915, July 2026) is a KiCad-native routing environment with 679 real open-source boards and two synthetic generators; its reinforcement-learning routers, trained on synthetic boards against KiCad's DRC, approach a rule-based router without beating it. No published application of a JEPA to board or chip placement or routing exists.

**What the pipeline does right by that rubric.**
1. No language model decides geometry: every coordinate comes from a generator, every track from Freerouting or a DRC-gated Python pass; routeflow never edits a generator and never composes a command from model text (`routeflow-methodology.md` line 22). The session's job is the senior engineer's: read the audit image, change a constraint in the generator, rerun.
2. Verdicts are mechanical and fail closed: hard, unrouted, vias and pair skew come from the DRC JSON and the gates, missing artefacts block, the journal is append-only and keyed by the pre-route hash, and the pre-registered 1.9.0 against 2.4.1 A/B was allowed to return NOT MET (`bench/report.md`).
3. The design is data and the generator is the record: twelve cross-board contracts from netlists (`check_contracts.py`, the TX_INHIBIT_n path to the KEY gate among them), one source for the plate and the backer (`panel1450.py`), intent checks where a bug bought them (every PCIe net reaches its switch, the PowerPAK pin map, the D8 RF chain net map, the zone-net gate).
4. The bar is stated honestly: the repository never says "fab ready" or "100 percent confidence" (grep: zero hits); its operative word is CLEAN (gate ALL PASS on the filled board, 0 unrouted, 0 of six hard DRC types, pairs within 1 mm) plus a fresh-eyes review at a stated confidence, and section 27.6 already records that every gate validated the design and never the deliverable.
5. Router knobs were measured and not believed (236 bench rows, the settings-block trap of the methodology's section 8), and the parallelism research reached the conclusion the interview implies: the win is in decomposing the problem, not in more machines.

**What it does wrong by the same rubric.**
1. **No electrical property is computed anywhere.** Impedance, crosstalk, DC drop and current density, thermal, return-path continuity, via stub length, per-net via budgets and EMC are all absent (grep-verified; the only "impedance" strings are prose in `export_jlc.sh` line 43 and `make_handoff.py` lines 51 to 56 asking JLC to tune for 90 ohm). CLEAN therefore means manufacturable and connected as drawn, the interview's junior first pass, not its computed verdict. The programme that would close this, MESHSAT-818, is scheduled "when the owner schedules it" with no verification criteria written. The consequence already shipped: the D8 deliverable's BOM carries the string "values to be verified in MESHSAT-818" as the value of its PA harmonic filter inductor (`v2/release/revA/boards/meshsat-pcb-d-revA-D8/pcb-d-aprs-bom.csv` line 29).
2. **Design intent is not data.** The schematic generators emit reference, symbol, value, footprint and a pin-to-net map; there is no "this capacitor bypasses that pin", no current per net, no impedance per pair class, no expected rail voltage. Those numbers live in comments and in the prose of 32.55, so no gate can read them, and the decoupling capacitors are shelf-packed into a hand-drawn rectangle by reference-number range (`gen_pcb_b3.py` lines 96 to 104) with no proximity rule.
3. **Placement has no objective and no feedback instrument short of a full route.** `FIXED` literals plus a left-to-right shelf packer sorted fine-pitch first and then by area (`gen_pcb_b3.py` lines 150 to 171); no wire length, no loop area, no escape-fan prediction. The loop exists but costs a route each turn: the A22 INA226 row was spaced at 12 mm after run 11 found two 0.5 mm MSOP fans colliding (`gen_pcb_a3.py` line 65); B16's HDMI switches at 9.6 mm pitch were found after a 3 h 20 min route. The interview's hourly cadence needs a minute-scale predictor before the router.
4. **Four gates are disarmed or dropped** (verified 8 Sep 00:50): (a) `check_zone_nets.py` can never block a chain, because `... | grep -E "FAIL|zone nets" || echo BLOCK` (`full_a22.sh` line 32 and the same line in `full_b16.sh`, `full_d8.sh`, `full_e6.sh`, `full_p1.sh`) always matches the summary line, so the block branch is dead code, and `full_c7.sh` does not run the gate at all; only routeflow's `^FAIL` regex catches it, and the chains also run standalone. (b) ERC never blocks: `build_sch.sh` line 5 turns the exit code into an echo and `full_a22.sh` line 10 only greps the log. (c) `check_contracts.py`, the best electrical check in the repository, is called by no chain, finish or routeflow profile. (d) The A21 gate's power-copper checks (band contiguity, stitch vias in fill, piece touching) were dropped in the A22 rewrite (`check_pcb_a.py` has no `band` or `stitch` line) while `finish_a22.sh` line 36 still greps for them and the gate's own comment at line 64 defers the currents to "the A23 power-copper pass"; A22 is the 20 A board. Beyond the four: the error-severity DRC types KiCad computes under `--severity-all` beyond the six hard ones (`solder_mask_bridge`, `annular_width`, `track_width`, `starved_thermal`, `diff_pair_gap_out_of_range`, `zones_intersect`, and `connection_width` as a warning) are discarded by every consumer; the courtyard rules are set to `ignore` in every project file; `finish_board.sh` runs without `set -e` and copies with `2>/dev/null`, which is how the 6 Sep deliverable lost its gerber zip.
5. **The reviewer that finds the real bugs is a session, not a gate.** Audit rounds 6 to 11 were gateway sessions reading documents; the substantive catches of the record (gerber zips without inner layers, 25.12; phantom-net pours, 32.33; net classes never applied, 32.39; SOT-23 pin swaps, 32.36; the TPS2065 package) were each found by a reading session and became a gate only afterwards, one by one. The interview's model is the reverse: the evaluator is built first and the solver is judged against it.
6. **Smaller blind spots** (critic pass, verified 00:58): `escape_prune.py` (`full_b16.sh` line 24) removes any escape stub that sits in a hard violation and hands the pad to the router with only a count printed, so a 0.4 mm receptacle pad can lose its only via site with nothing checking the router gave it one (the A19 SDA case); the six-layer B16 board file carries no dielectric or epsilon entry, so the 100 ohm order note is unconnected to any geometry in the project; the pair report of `check_pcb_b.py` lines 89 to 95 lists only pairs whose both legs have tracks, so a pair with one leg unrouted is invisible to it and to `pair_match.sh`; `lcsc_fill.py` line 90 prints its blank count and exits 0 whatever the count.
7. **Deliverable properties are never read back**: no script checks a gerber zip against the layer count, the CPL origin or side column, the drill file, or BOM procurability (JLC's parts API of 32.54 is not called at order time); `make_handoff.py` only checks that the zip exists. The five properties of 27.2 are still read by no gate.

**On different models, and on JEPA.** The interview's own answer applies: an LLM reads datasheets and writes the generators and gates (what this project does), a specialised solver does geometry, and the evaluator is the asset. Quilter trains reinforcement learning against a physics engine it wrote in JAX and never on human designs; PCBWorld's routers approach a rule-based router without beating it; Freerouting stays the router here. The one learnable question in this pipeline, "where will the router fail given this placement", is a mature supervised field in chip design (RouteNet 2018, PGNN 2022, U-Nets on pin-density maps trained on 26,000 labelled placements) and nobody does it self-supervised. A JEPA pays when unlabeled data is abundant and labels are scarce; here the corpus is six base boards, 34 board-file revisions and 236 bench rows, and labels are cheap because the router is deterministic and the CPU box routes 76 small boards at once, so a night of jittered placements yields thousands of labelled samples for about 10 USD. What is scarce is board diversity, which no self-supervised objective creates. **Advice given and ruled (owner, 8 Sep 2026 about 01:05): not JEPA, not now, and no paid solver ("we have no money").** The condition under which a JEPA becomes the right tool is recorded: a corpus of thousands of distinct boards (PCBWorld's 679 plus its generators) and a slow evaluator producing few labels (openEMS at hours per pair), at which point an encoder pretrained on the unlabeled corpus and probed with few labels is textbook.

**What not to adopt from the interview.** Its bar describes a board a human reviewed for a week; nobody has looked at these boards with a human eye and nothing is built, so the bar to state is "every property the design claims is computed and recorded", not a borrowed phrase and not "100 percent confidence", which no method delivers. Rooms and hints as a user interface would be a second source of truth beside the generators. The session is not the senior engineer: deterministic solvers decide, the session proposes and records, the owner rules, and the fresh-eyes review never becomes a confidence number. Reinforcement-learned routing itself: the interview's figures do not beat the pipeline's 0-open finishes on five of six boards; the lesson is the evaluator, not the agent.

**The programme (MESHSAT-862, plan file on the runner `~/.claude/plans/smooth-napping-cookie.md`; ruled scope: audit, gate repairs, electrical layer, placement predictor, a learned-critic experiment without a JEPA arm, from the vast.ai credit).** Stage B, re-arm the gates: the zone-net gate, ERC and `check_contracts.py` block every chain and finish; the A21 power-copper checks return for A22, B16 and P1; one shared hard set (`tools/hardset.py`) that adds `solder_mask_bridge`, `annular_width`, `track_width`, `diff_pair_gap_out_of_range`, `zones_intersect` and `courtyards_overlap`; `finish_board.sh` asserts every deliverable item and reads the gerber zip back against the layer count; the pruned escapes are gated; the pair report lists one-leg pairs; `lcsc_fill.py` fails above an allow-listed blank count; the JLC stackups are written into every project; one refusing selftest per re-armed gate; every pre-route chain rerun on the box with the counts recorded here. Stage C, the intent file per board from the schematic generators (bypass pin, rail currents, pair classes) and the electrical verdicts as gates: `dc_drop.py` (resistive mesh, 2 percent budget, IPC-2221 internal density) on A22, B16, P1 and E6; `impedance_check.py` (analytical from the project stackup, 10 percent) on every pair with openEMS only on the failing ones; return-path and decoupling-loop gates; SPICE and thermal numbers into the record. Stage D, `place_audit.py` inside every chain (pin density, escape-fan collision, HPWL, decoupling loops, a PNG), required to predict the two recorded collisions from the boards in history and none on the released A22. Stage E, the learned critic: a jitter data campaign on the CPU box, the analytical arm against a supervised U-Net on a held-out board, then placement search judged by the router; `v2/docs/research-learned-critic.md` and 32.65 with the numbers, negative results recorded as results.

**The running B16 campaign (assessment 01:06, given to the owner, who instructs that session).** The campaign has established that the B16 pre-route board flattens near 70 opens whatever the pass count (252, 159, 77, 74 at 3, 5, 12, 16 passes), and 32.63 names the cause as placement (the HDMI switches at 9.6 mm pitch; about 500 interleaved rail pads that need a placement pass, owed as B17). The from-scratch 30 to 60-pass runs therefore buy passes against a condemned placement; the net-partition result is a methodology result worth finishing; the p3 to p16 boards, their DRC JSONs and the journal are labelled data for Stages D and E; a B16 finish, hand closures or release on this placement would be the hand-patched junior board this audit argues against; B17 is judged once by the gates of Stages C and D.

**Owner rulings still needed at execution time (one per question):** whether Stage C runs before B16's release or after it (a failed drop gate regenerates A22 or B16); whether "100 percent confidence" means the interview's bar (computed verdicts on every electrical property the design names, plus the built-kit test plan of `TEST-PLAN.md`) or more; the record will carry the definition verbatim.

## 32.65 B16 route campaign stopped on this placement; the net-partition result (8 Sep 2026, 01:19 CEST)

**Stop.** At 23:19 UTC (01:19 CEST) every Freerouting process on box 50107044 was killed by PID on the owner's ruling relayed from the fab-ready-board-audit session (MESHSAT-862): the 30, 40 and 60-pass from-scratch runs (started 18:45 and 20:33 UTC, none had reached a session), the two 10-pass region hedges, and routeflow's round 2 (100 passes, 8 h limit, from 14:46 UTC). B16 is held on this placement: no finish, no hand closures, no deliverable, no release. The partition reconcile was allowed to finish for its numbers. Every routed board, session, DRC file and log of the day is kept as labelled data for the placement predictor of MESHSAT-862 (`/home/claude-runner/meshsat-b16-route-data/`, `labels.csv`). B17, with the HDMI switch pitch and the interleaved rail pads fixed, waits for the owner's word and is judged once by the gates of 32.64.

**What the day measured on this placement (1452 connections after the plane fanout, four routing layers, Freerouting 1.9.0 single-threaded since its thread option touches only the optimizer).** From scratch: 3 passes 1 h 42 min, 2 hard, 252 open; 5 passes 2 h 05 min, 0 hard, 159 open; 12 passes 3 h 20 min, 0 hard, 77 open; 16 passes 3 h 43 min, 74 open; 20 passes 3 h 46 min, 65 open. The 12-pass board after the clean-up and the board-wide stub router: 0 hard, 29 open, of which 14 sit at the two HDMI switches U3 and U4 (TS3DV642, 0.4 mm pitch, 9.6 mm apart: an escape-fan collision of the kind A22's INA226 row had at 8 mm), 3 are the SWP2 Ethernet pairs from U1 at the west band to slot 2, 8 are plane pads without a via, the rest single signals. Runs with 100, 40, 20 and 10 passes under 4 h, 1 h 50 min, 3 h and 1 h 40 min limits wrote nothing; the router writes its session only after the last pass.

**The net partition (tools `dsn_partition.py`, `route_part.sh`, `dsn_export.sh`, `ses_import_lock.py`, `ses_merge.py`, `part_stage2.sh`, `part_reconcile.sh`; research note `v2/docs/research-parallel-autorouting.md`).** Stage 1, the global nets (145 nets, about 330 wire connections plus the plane nets) with every region class ignored: 20 passes in 33 minutes, 0 hard, 1 wire open (HDMI2_CK_N) and 45 plane pads without a via (34 ground, 11 rail), the tracks locked. Stage 2, the five regions concurrently against the locked global tracks, 20 passes each: the west band 3.5 min, slot 2 49 min, slot 1 66 min, the east band 96 min, slot 3 104 min. The merge by net gave 16,883 items and 537 merged nets, and 374 crossings, 199 shorts and 500 clearance violations between regions (slot 2 against slot 3 367, the east band against slot 3 209, slot 1 against slot 2 175, slot 1 against slot 3 88, the rest smaller), concentrated between x -66 and +66 of the case frame: a region job sees the other columns as free space and routes through them, so unconfined concurrent jobs collide wherever their detours meet. The unknot rip of the conflicts left 11 hard and 450 open before the stub router. Lessons for the next use of the scheme: confine each region job with keep-outs over the other columns' cores on the routing layers and put every net that touches a margin into the global group (that partition is 175 global nets against 140, 142, 132, 38 and 55 in the regions), then a short all-class continuation for the leftovers; keep the project file beside every board KiCad checks (without it the DRC reports the default class: 536 false clearance and 199 false via-size violations on the first stage-1 check); and bash's `GROUPS` is a read-only array, a group list must not be named so. The stage-1 timing stands as the useful number: a third of the board's connections route in a thirtieth of the time the whole board needs for the same pass count.

**Close of the campaign (01:30 CEST).** The reconcile's stub router had closed 19 of the 450 openings in twelve minutes and was stopped; the merged and reconciled board stands at 11 hard (9 clearance) and 450 open (`partition/part/rec-final.json` in the data set). Nothing runs on box 50107044; the data set (131 files: the pre-route board and DSN, the 3, 5, 12, 16 and 20-pass boards with their sessions and DRC files, the thread tests, the partition stages, the diagnostics, every log, `labels.csv`) is on the runner and the box is destroyed after this entry. The confinement of region jobs is in the tools (`dsn_confine.py`, `route_part.sh` with `CONFINE=1`, `dsn_partition.py --strict=8`, commit ec193b2) for B17, untested on a route.
### 32.66 The re-armed gates and the electrical verdicts on the released boards (8 Sep 2026, 02:30 CEST; MESHSAT-862 Stages B, C and D; box 50212913)

**What ran.** Every number below was produced on the rented CPU box (16 threads, 0.06 USD per hour; KiCad 9.0.9 with the symbol and footprint libraries, scipy) by the scripts named, on copies of the released deliverables (`v2/release/revA/boards/`) and on fresh generations of the six pre-route boards in copies inside `v2/ecad/`; the released project directories and the sibling session's B16 data were not touched. The gateway session `meshsat-4b` wrote the register of dead gate lines (`/home/claude-runner/MESHSAT-862-gate-register.md`, 12 classes, all folded into Stage B) and the gateway session `meshsat-f4` the tool review (`/home/claude-runner/MESHSAT-862-tool-review.md`, 5 blockers, 5 high, 17 medium, all applied); neither could run anything.

**Stage B, the gates as they stand (c588047 and this section's commit).** One hard set of fifteen DRC types in `tools/hardset.py` for every chain, finish, wrapper and the router's own score (the register had found four different sets: `tracks_crossing` in no pre-route set, `courtyards_overlap`, `via_diameter`, `drill_out_of_range` and `items_not_allowed` in no post-route set); the own-courtyard overlap and the same-footprint mask bridge are the only exemptions. The dead lines: the zone-net gate's `|| echo BLOCK` (five chains; C7 had no gate), ERC's exit code turned into an echo, `check_contracts.py` called by nothing, the A21 power-copper checks dropped from the A22 gate, the pair gate of the A22 and B16 finishes testing `cut`'s status so that the owner's 5 Sep 17:00 ruling had never fired, chains exiting 0 on their own BLOCK, no finish deleting its clean flag, a stub-router crash as an echo, `finish_board.sh` copying with the error discarded, `lcsc_fill.py` and `escape_prune.py` reporting and exiting 0: all re-armed. New gates: `erc_gate.py` (errors block unless `<project>/erc-allow.txt` gives a reason per line), `verify_deliverable.py` (every deliverable item, the gerber zip against the copper count, BOM and CPL form and designators; a refused folder is removed), `stackup_write.py` (no project had any stackup, dielectric or epsilon: the JLC04161H-7628 and JLC06161H-3313 stacks are now in every board file), `copper_checks.py` (pour pieces anchored by a pad or via, fill against the outline area, locked vias in fill, cross-layer links through vias and through-hole pads), `pruned_gate.py`, the intent gates below, `check_contracts.py` before every clean flag. `routeflow.py` removes the clean flag before the finish, requires `contracts: ALL PASS`, and its selftest holds 43 predicates. `export_jlc.sh` writes real designators: every released BOM carried `J_ANT?`-style references (kicad-cli marks a reference without a number) and `C49-C57` ranges, which the deliverable read-back now refuses.

**Stage C, the electrical verdicts on the released boards (closed-form, the analytical model; openEMS is the refinement, not the source of these findings).**
1. **Every differential pair on every released board is uncoupled.** `impedance_check.py` measures the gap between the legs along the route: A22's USB_D8, USB_E6 and USB_WALL legs run 2.4, 5.3 and 2.8 mm apart at 0.20 mm width on In2 and In3; C7's USB_PNL 2.3 mm apart; D8's USB1, USB2, USB3 9.6, 2.7 and 2.1 mm apart and USB_D8 0.31 mm apart but unreferenced over 9.8 mm; E6's USB_E6 likewise. Freerouting has no differential-pair routing; the generators set the pair gap in the net class and the router never read it; `meander.py` matched lengths and nothing coupled. The order notes' "USB pairs 0.20/0.15 mm (90 ohm)" described a geometry that was never routed: the legs are lone 0.20 mm traces at about 104 ohm single-ended on the inner layers (the model gives 2 x 104 = 208 ohm as a pair, which is the uncoupled limit). For the stack geometries themselves the model puts the outer-layer 0.20/0.15 USB pair on the 7628 stack at about 102 ohm (13 percent above 90; the closed form ignores the mask and over-predicts at s/h 0.7, so openEMS decides) and a 0.127/0.127 stripline pair on the 3313 stack at about 74 ohm against 100 (26 percent, outside the model's band: with about 0.1 mm to each plane no width reaches 100 ohm on that layer pair, a layer-assignment question for B16's PCIe and HDMI, not a geometry one). Remedy in the tools: `pair_shadow.py` rebuilds the N leg as an offset copy of the routed P leg at the class gap, DRC-gated (written, first test on A22's USB_D8 pending).
2. **Return paths.** `intent_checks.py` samples every pair-class track for a filled plane on a neighbouring copper layer; the limit is 5 percent of the net's length or 10 mm, whichever is larger (connector anti-pads and via transitions sit over nothing). C7: USB_DP_R, USB_DM_R, USB_PNL_P, USB_PNL_N run 23.7 of 44.2, 8.9 of 43.2, 26.0 of 486 and 66.3 of 515 mm without a reference (the backer's In1 GND plane references F.Cu and In2 only; a track on B.Cu of the four-layer stack has In2 next to it, which carries no plane). D8: 9 nets of the USB hub over the limit (22 with any gap at all; the hub's D+ and D- lines run 30 to 60 percent of their length on B.Cu without a plane). E6: 1. A22's six-layer stack references every layer; its 19 nets show 3 to 9 percent at the connector ends and the ten RF site stubs 3.6 of 10 mm (the SMP-MAX to SMA link over the site's plane cut-out), one over the limit.
3. **DC drop (`dc_drop.py`, a 0.5 mm resistive mesh of the rail's own copper, the intent currents, the drop as the verdict; the current density at a one-cell neck overstates and is reported only).** A22, 1 of 12 rails within the 2 percent budget: VBAT 770 mV (5.35 percent of 14.4 V at 10 A), CELL+ 213 mV (1.48 percent, the locked bars and the 9 A pins), VIN_RAW 1300 mV (10.8 percent at 8 A, 99 percent of the current on In2), VBUS20 136 mV (0.68 percent), +5V_S1, S2, S3 327, 446 and 547 mV (6.4, 8.8 and 10.7 percent of 5.1 V at 5 A, 80 to 90 percent of the current on In2 router tracks), +5V_DEV 292 mV (5.8 percent), +3V3 49 mV (1.5 percent), +13V8_PA 1810 mV (13.1 percent of 13.8 V at 6 A), +12V_HF 230 mV (1.9 percent), +54V_POE 47 mV (0.09 percent, MET). The mechanism is the one the A21 rule named and the A22 gate deferred ("the A23 power-copper pass carries the currents", `check_pcb_a.py` line 64): on A22 the slot rails, the PA rail and the vehicle input travel in 0.4 mm router tracks on the 0.5 oz inner layer In2, and a 0.4 mm track of 15 um copper over 100 mm is about 0.3 ohm. C7's +5V at 0.6 A: 252 mV, 5.04 percent, on a long 0.25 mm track from the ribbon to the far strip. D8's +5V_D8 at 1 A: 97 mV, 1.94 percent, MET (the first pass had called three load pads unconnected, a mesh that did not link layers through through-hole barrels: fixed). E6: CELL_F 15 mV (0.10 percent at 10 A through its pour, band and In2 plane) and VIN_RAW 222 mV (1.85 percent at 8 A), both MET. P1: PACK_P 26 mV, CELL4 264 mV (1.84 percent), FUSED 16 mV at 10 A, all MET: the locked bands of the pack board carry their current. With the drop as the verdict A22 stands at 5 of 12 rails MET (CELL+, VBUS20, +3V3, +12V_HF, +54V_POE).
4. The deliverable read-back on the released folders: every one fails on its BOM designators (fixed at the source) and on the missing BOM status file; E5 passes in bare-board mode (19 of 19 properties).

**Stage D, the placement instrument.** The first version grew an envelope around each fine-pitch part by a fitted constant and was wrong twice: its pad test used the wrong enum value (the review's B1) and, once fixed, it predicted collisions on boards that routed clean (C7 8 of 8 parts, A22 10 of 19). The version that stands measures instead of guessing: it runs after `escape.py`, `join_adjacent_pins.py` and `prefanout.py`, and reads the escape fans the board carries: a fine-pitch pad without an escape (skipped by the escape pass, or a part excluded by `ESCAPE_SKIP` within 6 mm of another fine-pitch part), two parts' locked-copper envelopes overlapping by more than 0.3 mm on both axes, and any escape the pre-route DRC pruned.
